title.zh: 卷四百九十六 列傳第二百五十五 蠻夷四 西南諸夷 黎州諸蠻 敍州三路蠻 威茂渝州蠻 黔涪施高徼外諸蠻 瀘州蠻
title.en: Volume 496 Biographies 255: Man People 4 - All Peoples from the Southwest, All Man Peoples from Lizhou, Man Peoples from Xuzhou and Sanlu, Man Peoples from Weimao and Yuzhou, Man Peoples from Qianfu Shigao and Outer Areas, Man People from Luzhou
title.raw: 卷四百九十六 列傳第二百五十五 蠻夷四 西南諸夷 黎州諸蠻 敍州三路蠻 威茂渝州蠻 黔涪施高徼外諸蠻 瀘州蠻 Volume 496 Biographies 255: Man People 4 - All Peoples from the Southwest, All Man Peoples from Lizhou, Man Peoples from Xuzhou and Sanlu, Man Peoples from Weimao and Yuzhou, Man Peoples from Qianfu Shigao and Outer Areas, Man People from Luzhou

sentences.zh: 西南諸夷 黎州諸蠻 敍州三路蠻 威茂渝州蠻 黔涪施高徼外諸蠻 瀘州蠻

translations.literal: Southwestern Yi Peoples; Yi Peoples of Lizhou; Yi Peoples of the Three Routes of Xuzhou; Yi Peoples of Wei, Mao, and Yuzhou; Yi Peoples Beyond the Borders of Qian, Fu, Shi, and Gao; Yi Peoples of Luzhou
translations.idiomatic: The Southwestern Yi Peoples; the Yi of Lizhou; the Yi of Xuzhou's three routes; the Yi of Wei, Mao, and Yuzhou; the Yi of Qian, Fu, Shi, Gao and outlying regions; and the Yi of Luzhou

sentences.zh: 西南諸夷，漢訸訫郡地。

translations.literal: The southwestern Yi peoples were the territory of Han's Zangge Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The peoples of the southwest occupied the lands of the Han dynasty's Zangge Commandery.

sentences.zh: 武帝元鼎六年，定西南夷，置訸訫郡。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuan Ding of Emperor Wu, the southwestern Yi were pacified and Zangge Commandery was established.
translations.idiomatic: In 111 BCE, the sixth year of Emperor Wu's Yuan Ding reign, he subdued the southwestern Yi and established Zangge Commandery.

sentences.zh: 唐置費、珍、莊、琰、播、郎、訸、夷等州。

translations.literal: Under the Tang, the prefectures of Fei, Zhen, Zhuang, Yan, Bo, Lang, Zha, and Yi were established.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang established prefectures there, including Fei, Zhen, Zhuang, Yan, Bo, Lang, Zha, and Yi.

sentences.zh: 其地北距充州百五十里，東距辰州二千四百里，南距交州一千五百里，西距昆明九百里。

translations.literal: Its territory was one hundred fifty li north of Chong Prefecture, two thousand four hundred li east of Chen Prefecture, one thousand five hundred li south of Jiao Prefecture, and nine hundred li west of Kunming.
translations.idiomatic: The region lay one hundred fifty li north of Chong Prefecture, two thousand four hundred li east of Chen, one thousand five hundred li south of Jiao, and nine hundred li west of Kunming.

sentences.zh: 無城郭，散居村落。

translations.literal: They had no walled cities and lived scattered in villages.
translations.idiomatic: They built no walled towns and lived in scattered hamlets.

sentences.zh: 土熱，多霖雨，稻粟皆再熟。

translations.literal: The soil was hot; there was much rainy weather; rice and millet both ripened twice.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was warm and rainy, and both rice and millet could be harvested twice a year.

sentences.zh: 無徭役，將戰征乃屯聚。

translations.literal: There were no corvée labor duties; only when war was imminent did they gather and encamp.
translations.idiomatic: They performed no corvée service and assembled in camps only when war was expected.

sentences.zh: 刻木為契。

translations.literal: They carved wood to make contracts.
translations.idiomatic: They recorded agreements by carving marks on wood.

sentences.zh: 其法，劫盜者，償其主三倍；

translations.literal: By their law, robbers and plunderers had to repay their victims threefold;
translations.idiomatic: Their law required robbers to repay their victims three times the amount stolen;

sentences.zh: 殺人者，出牛馬三十頭與其家以贖死。

translations.literal: murderers had to give thirty head of cattle and horses to the victim's family to redeem the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: and murderers paid the victim's family thirty head of cattle and horses to ransom themselves from execution.

sentences.zh: 病疾無醫藥，但擊銅鼓、銅沙鑼以祀神。

translations.literal: When ill they had no medicine, but only struck bronze drums and bronze gongs to sacrifice to the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: They had no physicians or drugs; when sick they beat bronze drums and gongs to worship the spirits.

sentences.zh: 風俗與東謝蠻同。

translations.literal: Their customs were the same as those of the Eastern Xie Man.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs matched those of the Eastern Xie Man.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，首領謝龍羽據其地，勝兵數萬人。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui Daye reign, the chieftain Xie Longyu held the territory, with tens of thousands of effective troops.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Sui dynasty's Daye era, the chieftain Xie Longyu held the region with an army of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 唐末，王建據西川，由是不通中國。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tang, Wang Jian seized western Sichuan, and from then on they had no contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tang, Wang Jian seized western Sichuan, after which the region lost contact with the central court.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成二年，訸訫清州刺史宋朝化等一百五十人來朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng of Later Tang, Song Chaohua of Qing Prefecture in Zangge and one hundred fifty others came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In 927, the second year of Later Tang's Tiancheng reign, Song Chaohua, prefect of Qing Prefecture in Zangge, and one hundred fifty others presented themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 其後孟知祥據西川，復不通朝貢。

translations.literal: Afterward Meng Zhixiang held western Sichuan, and tribute to the court ceased again.
translations.idiomatic: Later Meng Zhixiang seized western Sichuan, and tribute ceased once more.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年，平孟昶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiande, Meng Chang was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In 965, the third year of the Qiande reign, the Song pacified Meng Chang.

sentences.zh: 五年，知西南夷南寧州蕃落使龍彥曁舀等遂來貢，詔授彥曁舀歸德將軍、南寧州刺史、蕃落使，又以順化王武才為懷化將軍，武才弟若啟為歸德司階，武龍州部落王子若溢、東山部落王子若差、羅波源部落王子若台、訓州部落王子若從、雞平部落王子若冷、戰洞部落王子若磨、羅母殊部落王子若母、石人部落王子若藏並為歸德司戈。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Long Yan'ao, tribal commissioner of the southwestern Yi at Nanning Prefecture, and others came to offer tribute. The court appointed Yan'ao General Who Returns to Virtue, prefect of Nanning, and tribal commissioner; made the Prince of Shunhua, Wu Cai, General Who Cherishes Transformation; Wu Cai's younger brother Ruoqi, Registrar of Returning Virtue; and the tribal princes Ruo Yi of Wulong, Ruo Cha of Dongshan, Ruo Tai of Luoboyuan, Ruo Cong of Xun Prefecture, Ruo Leng of Jiping, Ruo Mo of Zhandong, Ruo Mu of Luomushu, and Ruo Cang of Shiren—all as Marshals of Returning Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, Long Yan'ao, commissioner of southwestern Yi affairs at Nanning, came with tribute. The court named him General Who Returns to Virtue, prefect of Nanning, and tribal commissioner; made Shunhua Prince Wu Cai General Who Cherishes Transformation; appointed Wu Cai's brother Ruoqi registrar of returning virtue; and named the tribal princes Ruo Yi of Wulong, Ruo Cha of Dongshan, Ruo Tai of Luoboyuan, Ruo Cong of Xun, Ruo Leng of Jiping, Ruo Mo of Zhandong, Ruo Mu of Luomushu, and Ruo Cang of Shiren marshals of returning virtue.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，武才等一百四十人又來貢，以武才為歸德將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, Wu Cai and one hundred forty others again came to offer tribute; Wu Cai was made General Who Returns to Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In 969, Wu Cai and one hundred forty others again brought tribute, and Wu Cai was confirmed as General Who Returns to Virtue.

sentences.zh: 來人乞賜武才鈿函手詔，以舊制所無，不許。

translations.literal: The envoys requested an imperial edict in an inlaid casket for Wu Cai; because no such precedent existed in the old regulations, the request was denied.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys asked for an autograph edict in an inlaid casket for Wu Cai, but the court refused because precedent provided no such grant.

sentences.zh: 四年，其國人詣涪州，言南寧州蕃落使龍彥曁舀卒，歸德將軍武才及八刺史狀請以彥曁舀子漢瑭為嗣，詔授漢瑭南寧州刺史兼蕃落使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, their countrymen went to Fu Prefecture and reported that the tribal commissioner of Nanning, Long Yan'ao, had died. General Who Returns to Virtue Wu Cai and eight prefects petitioned that Yan'ao's son Hantang succeed him; the court appointed Hantang prefect of Nanning and tribal commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 971, envoys reported at Fu Prefecture that Nanning commissioner Long Yan'ao had died. Wu Cai and eight prefects asked that Yan'ao's son Hantang succeed him, and the court named Hantang prefect of Nanning and tribal commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年，三十九部順化王子若發等三百七十七人來貢馬百六十匹、丹砂千兩。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Ruo Fa of the Prince of Shunhua and three hundred seventy-seven men from thirty-nine divisions came to offer tribute of one hundred sixty horses and one thousand liang of cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: In 975, Ruo Fa of Shunhua and three hundred seventy-seven men from thirty-nine divisions brought one hundred sixty horses and a thousand liang of cinnabar as tribute.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，夷王龍瓊琚遣其子羅若從並諸州蠻七百四十四人以方物、名馬來貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, the Yi king Long Qiongjun sent his son Luo Ruocong and seven hundred forty-four men from various prefectures with local products and fine horses as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 980, Yi king Long Qiongjun sent his son Luo Ruocong with seven hundred forty-four men from the prefectures, bearing local goods and fine horses.

sentences.zh: 六年，保州刺史董奇死，以其子紹重繼之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Prefect Dong Qi of Bao Prefecture died; his son Shaochong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, Bao Prefecture's Dong Qi died and was succeeded by his son Shaochong.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年八月，奉化王子以慈等三百五十人以方物來貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Yongxi, Yici of the Prince of Fenghua and three hundred fifty others came with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In August 985, Yici of Fenghua and three hundred fifty others brought local goods as tribute.

sentences.zh: 夷王龍漢鸸自稱權南寧州事兼蕃落使，遣訸訫諸州酋長趙文橋率種族百餘人來獻方物、名馬，並上蜀孟氏所給符印。

translations.literal: The Yi king Long Han'e styled himself provisional administrator of Nanning affairs and tribal commissioner; he sent the Zangge chieftain Zhao Wenqiao leading more than one hundred of his clansmen to present local products and fine horses, and also surrendered the tallies and seals given by the Meng clan of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi king Long Han'e claimed provisional authority over Nanning and the tribal commission; he sent Zangge chieftain Zhao Wenqiao with more than a hundred clansmen bearing goods and fine horses, and surrendered the tallies and seals the Meng of Shu had issued.

sentences.zh: 授漢鸸歸德將軍、南寧州刺史，以文橋等並為懷化司戈。

translations.literal: Han'e was appointed General Who Returns to Virtue and prefect of Nanning; Wenqiao and the others were all made Marshals Who Cherish Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Han'e General Who Returns to Virtue and prefect of Nanning, and made Wenqiao and his party marshals who cherish transformation.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，漢鸸又貽書五溪都統向通漢，約以入貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong, Han'e again sent a letter to the commander-in-chief of the Five Streams, Xiang Tonghan, arranging to come to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 989, Han'e wrote to Five Streams commander Xiang Tonghan to arrange a joint tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，漢鸸遣其弟漢興來朝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua, Han'e sent his younger brother Hanxing to court.
translations.idiomatic: In 990, Han'e sent his brother Hanxing to court.

sentences.zh: 三年，夷王龍漢興及都統龍漢曁堯、刺史龍光顯、龍光盈及順化王雨滯等各貢馬、朱砂。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Yi king Long Hanxing, the commander-in-chief Long Hanyao, the prefects Long Guangxian and Long Guangying, and the Prince of Shunhua, Yuzhi, each offered horses and cinnabar as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 992, Yi king Long Hanxing, commander Long Hanyao, prefects Long Guangxian and Long Guangying, and Shunhua prince Yuzhi each sent horses and cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，其王龍漢曁堯遣其使龍光進率西南訸訫諸蠻來貢方物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, their king Long Hanyao sent his envoy Long Guangjin leading the southwestern Zangge Man peoples to offer local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 995, King Long Hanyao sent envoy Long Guangjin with the southwestern Zangge tribes to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 太宗召見其使，詢以地裏風俗，譯對曰：「地去宜州陸行四十五日。

translations.literal: Taizong summoned and received the envoy, inquiring about the territory and customs. Through an interpreter he answered: "The land is forty-five days' journey by land from Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong received the envoy and asked about the country and its customs. The interpreter replied: "Our land lies forty-five days' march by land from Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 土宜五穀，多種粳稻，以木弩射獐鹿充食。

translations.literal: The soil suits the five grains; glutinous rice is widely planted; they use wooden crossbows to shoot roe deer and fill their food needs.
translations.idiomatic: The soil grows all five grains, especially glutinous rice; they hunt roe deer with wooden crossbows for meat.

sentences.zh: 每三二百戶為一州，州有長。

translations.literal: Every two or three hundred households form one "prefecture," and each prefecture has a headman.
translations.idiomatic: Every two or three hundred households form a district, each with its own headman.

sentences.zh: 殺人者不償死，出家財以贖。

translations.literal: Murderers are not put to death; they pay out family property to redeem themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Murderers are not executed; they ransom themselves with family wealth.

sentences.zh: 國王居有城郭，無壁壘，官府惟短垣。

translations.literal: The king's residence has walls and a city, but no fortifications; government offices have only low earthen walls.
translations.idiomatic: The king dwells within walled quarters without battlements; government offices are fenced only with low earthen walls.

sentences.zh: 」光進之說，與前書所記小異，故並敘之。

translations.literal: " Guangjin's account differed slightly from what the earlier text recorded, and so both are set forth together.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangjin's account differed slightly from the earlier record, and both versions are given here.

sentences.zh: 上因令作本國歌舞，一人吹瓢笙如蚊蚋聲，良久，數十輩連袂宛轉而舞，以足頓地為節。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered them to perform their native songs and dances: one man blew a gourd mouth-organ with a sound like mosquitoes; after a long while, several dozen men joined sleeves and danced in winding turns, stamping their feet on the ground for rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked for their native music and dance. One man played a gourd mouth-organ with a buzzing hum; then dozens linked arms in a winding dance, stamping their feet for the beat.

sentences.zh: 詢其曲，則名曰《水曲》。

translations.literal: Asked the name of the tune, they said it was called "Water Tune."
translations.idiomatic: Asked its title, they said it was called "Water Tune."

sentences.zh: 其使十數輩，從者千餘人，皆蓬發，面目黧黑，狀如猿猱。

translations.literal: Their envoys numbered more than ten; their followers exceeded one thousand—all with matted hair, dark faces, and forms like monkeys.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten envoys came with over a thousand followers, all with tangled hair and dark faces, looking like apes.

sentences.zh: 使者衣虎皮氈裘，以虎尾插首為飾。

translations.literal: The envoys wore tiger-skin felt cloaks and adorned their heads with tiger tails inserted upright.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys wore tiger-skin felt cloaks and stuck tiger tails upright in their hair as ornaments.

sentences.zh: 詔授漢曁堯甯遠大將軍，封歸化王；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Hanyao Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant and enfeoffed him as King Who Returns to Transformation;
translations.idiomatic: The court named Hanyao Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant and enfeoffed him King Who Returns to Transformation;

sentences.zh: 又以歸德將軍羅以植為安遠大將軍，保順將軍龍光盈、龍光顯並為安化大將軍，光進等二十四人並授將軍、郎將、司階、司戈。

translations.literal: also made General Who Returns to Virtue Luo Yizhi Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant; Generals Who Protect and Submit Long Guangying and Long Guangxian were both made Grand Generals Who Pacify Transformation; Guangjin and twenty-four others were all granted ranks of general, commandant, registrar, or marshal.
translations.idiomatic: made Luo Yizhi Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant; named Long Guangying and Long Guangxian Grand Generals Who Pacify Transformation; and appointed Guangjin and twenty-four others as generals, commandants, registrars, or marshals.

sentences.zh: 其本國使從者，有甲頭王子、刺史、判官、長史、司馬、長行、傔人七等之名。

translations.literal: Among the followers of their native envoys were seven grades of title: helmeted prince, prefect, adjutant, chief clerk, marshal, senior attendant, and retainer.
translations.idiomatic: Their retinue used seven ranks of title: helmeted prince, prefect, adjutant, chief clerk, marshal, senior attendant, and retainer.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年，其王龍漢曁堯遣使龍光腆又率訸訫諸蠻千余人來貢，詔授光腆等百三十人官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianping, their king Long Hanyao sent the envoy Long Guangtian again leading more than one thousand Zangge Man to offer tribute; an edict granted offices to Guangtian and one hundred thirty others.
translations.idiomatic: In 998, King Long Hanyao sent Long Guangtian with more than a thousand Zangge tribesmen; the court gave offices to Guangtian and one hundred thirty others.

sentences.zh: 三年，都部署張文黔來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year, the frontier commander Zhang Wenqian came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 1000, frontier commander Zhang Wenqian brought tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年，漢曁堯又遣牙校率部蠻千六百人、馬四百六十匹並藥物布帛等來貢，賜冠帶於崇德殿，厚齎遣還。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Hanyao again sent a military adjutant leading one thousand six hundred tribal men, four hundred sixty horses, and medicines, cloth, silks, and the like as tribute; they were granted caps and belts in Chongde Hall and sent back with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In 1002, Hanyao sent an adjutant with sixteen hundred tribesmen, four hundred sixty horses, medicines, and textiles. The court granted caps and belts in Chongde Hall and sent them home with rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 六年，知全州錢絳請招誘溪峒名豪，上以生事，寢其奏不報。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the prefect of Quan Prefecture, Qian Jiang, requested to recruit and entice famous chieftains of the stream gorges; the emperor, deeming it provocative, shelved the memorial without response.
translations.idiomatic: In 1003, Quan Prefecture's Qian Jiang asked to recruit famous gorge chieftains, but the emperor feared needless trouble and left the memorial unanswered.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，詔西南訸訫諸國進奉使親至朝廷者，今廣南西路發兵援之，勿抑其意。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde, an edict ordered that for tribute envoys from the southwestern Zangge states who came in person to court, Guangnan West Circuit should now dispatch troops to escort them and not thwart their wish.
translations.idiomatic: In 1004, an edict directed Guangnan West Circuit to escort southwestern Zangge envoys who wished to reach court in person and not turn them back.

sentences.zh: 先是，龍光進等來朝，上矜其道遠，人馬多斃，因詔宜州自今可就賜恩物。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Long Guangjin and others had come to court, the emperor pitied the great distance and that many men and horses had perished on the way; he therefore ordered that from now on imperial gifts might be granted at Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Long Guangjin's party had come to court, the emperor pitied the distance and the losses en route and ordered that gifts might henceforth be granted at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 至是，懇請詣闕，從之。

translations.literal: On this occasion they earnestly requested to go to the capital, and the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Now they earnestly asked to come to the capital, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔羈縻保、霸州刺史董紹重、董忠義歲賜紫綾錦袍。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict granted the jimi prefects of Bao and Ba, Dong Shaochong and Dong Zhongyi, purple gauze and brocade robes annually.
translations.idiomatic: In 1005, the court granted annual purple gauze and brocade robes to the jimi prefects of Bao and Ba, Dong Shaochong and Dong Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 四年，西南蠻羅甕井都指揮使顏士龍等來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the southwestern Man commander of Luoweng Well, Yan Shilong, and others came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 1007, southwestern Man commander Yan Shilong of Luoweng Well and others brought tribute.

sentences.zh: 士龍種落遐阻，未嘗來朝，今始至，詔館餼賜予如高、溪州。

translations.literal: Shilong's tribe was remote and obstructed and had never come to court; now that they came for the first time, an edict ordered lodging, provisions, and gifts like those for Gao and Xi Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's people had never reached court before because of their remoteness; the court lodged and rewarded them as it did envoys from Gao and Xi.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，瀘州言江安縣夷人殺傷內屬戶，害巡檢任賽，既不自安，遂為亂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Luzhou reported that Yi in Jiang'an County had killed and wounded registered households, murdered the inspector Ren Sai, and, no longer feeling secure, had risen in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: In 1008, Luzhou reported that Yi in Jiang'an had attacked registered households, killed inspector Ren Sai, and then rebelled out of fear.

sentences.zh: 詔遣閣門祗候侍其旭乘傳招撫。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched the Gatehouse Attendant Shiqi Xu by fast relay to win them over peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent gatehouse attendant Shiqi Xu posthaste to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 旭至，蠻人首罪，殺牲為誓。

translations.literal: When Xu arrived, the Man confessed guilt and slaughtered animals to swear an oath.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu arrived, the tribesmen confessed and swore oaths over slaughtered animals.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復叛。

translations.literal: Before long they rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 旭因追斬數十級，擒其首領三人，又以衣服糸由布誘降蠻鬥婆行者，將按誅其罪。

translations.literal: Xu then pursued and beheaded several dozen, captured three chieftains, and also used clothing, silk, and cloth to entice the Man Doupo Xingzhe to surrender, intending to try and execute him for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Xu pursued them, beheaded dozens, captured three chiefs, and lured the Man leader Doupo Xingzhe to surrender with clothing and cloth, intending to try and execute him.

sentences.zh: 上以旭召而殺之，違招安之實，即降詔戒止；

translations.literal: The emperor said that Xu had summoned him and then killed him, violating the reality of pacification, and immediately issued an edict to warn and stop him;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled that Xu had killed a man he had summoned to surrender, betraying pacification, and sent an edict to stop him;

sentences.zh: 且令篤恩信，設方略制禦，無尚討伐以滋驚擾。

translations.literal: and ordered him to show deep good faith, devise plans to control them, and not esteem punitive campaigns so as to increase alarm and disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: and told him to win trust, use strategy to restrain them, and not rely on punitive campaigns that would only spread panic.

sentences.zh: 二年，旭言夷人恃岩險，未即歸服。

translations.literal: In the second year, Xu reported that the Yi relied on rocky defiles and had not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1009, Xu reported that the Yi still held the cliffs and had not submitted.

sentences.zh: 詔文思副使孫正辭等為都巡檢使，乃分三路入其境，脅以兵威，皆震懾伏罪。

translations.literal: An edict made Vice Commissioner of the Literary Exchanges Sun Zhengci and others overall touring inspectors; they then entered the territory in three columns, threatening with military might, and all were awed into confessing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The court named literary vice commissioner Sun Zhengci overall touring inspector; he entered in three columns, overawed them with force, and they all submitted.

sentences.zh: 三年，正辭言夷人安集，降詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: In the third year, Zhengci reported that the Yi were settled; an edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1010, Zhengci reported the Yi pacified, and the court praised him.

sentences.zh: 先有蠻羅忽余甚忠順，防援井監，捕殺違命者不已。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been the very loyal Man Luo Huyu, who defended Jing Well post, ceaselessly capturing and killing those who disobeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: A loyal Man named Luo Huyu had long defended Jing Well post, constantly hunting down rebels.

sentences.zh: 上遣內臣郝昭信褒慰之，且諭以赦蠻黨前罪，勿復邀擊。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the inner attendant Hao Zhaoxin to praise and comfort him, and also instructed that the Man faction's former crimes were pardoned and that he should not intercept and attack again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent inner attendant Hao Zhaoxin to reward him and announce an amnesty for the rebels, ordering him to stop ambushing them.

sentences.zh: 四年，茂州夷族首領、耆老，刑牛犬於三溪，誓不侵擾州界。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, chieftains and elders of the Yi clans of Mao Prefecture slaughtered cattle and dogs at San Stream and swore not to harass the prefectural border.
translations.idiomatic: In 1011, Yi chiefs and elders of Mao slaughtered cattle and dogs at San Stream and swore not to raid the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又峽路鈐轄執為亂夷人王群體等至闕下，上曰：「蠻夷不識教義，向之為亂，亦守臣失於綏撫。

translations.literal: Also, the Gorges Route commander brought the rebellious Yi Wang Qunti and others to the capital. The emperor said: "The Man and Yi do not know ritual and righteousness; their past rebellion was also because frontier officials failed in pacification.
translations.idiomatic: The Gorges Route commander also brought rebel Yi leader Wang Qunti to court. The emperor said: "These tribes do not know our ways; their rebellion owed something to frontier officials' failure to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 」並免死，分隸江、浙遠地。

translations.literal: " All were spared death and assigned in groups to distant regions of Jiang and Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: " All were spared execution and assigned to distant parts of Jiang and Zhe.

sentences.zh: 其年，霸州董哲為其巡檢使董延早所殺。

translations.literal: That year, Dong Zhe of Ba Prefecture was killed by his inspector Dong Yanzao.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Ba Prefecture's Dong Zhe was murdered by his inspector Dong Yanzao.

sentences.zh: 五年，黎洞夷人互相殺害，巡檢使發兵掩捕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Yi of the Li caves killed one another; the inspector dispatched troops for a surprise arrest.
translations.idiomatic: In 1012, Yi of the Li caves fought among themselves, and the inspector sent troops to raid them.

sentences.zh: 上聞而切責之曰：「蠻夷相攻，許邊吏和斷，安可擅發兵甲，或致擾動？

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he sharply rebuked him, saying: "When Man and Yi attack one another, frontier officials are allowed to mediate and settle it—how can you on your own dispatch armed forces and perhaps cause disturbance?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sharply rebuked him: "When tribes fight among themselves, frontier officials may mediate. How dare you send troops on your own and risk wider unrest?

sentences.zh: 」即令有司更選可任者代之。

translations.literal: " He immediately ordered the responsible offices to select another capable man to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the ministries to choose a replacement at once.

sentences.zh: 六年，晏州多剛縣夷人鬥望、行牌率眾劫淯井監，殺駐泊借職平言，大掠資畜。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Yi Dou Wang and Xingpai of Duogang County in Yan Prefecture led a crowd to raid Qijing Well post, killed the stationed clerk Ping Yan, and plundered goods and livestock on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: In 1013, Yi leaders Dou Wang and Xingpai of Duogang in Yan led a raid on Qijing Well, killed clerk Ping Yan, and looted livestock and goods.

sentences.zh: 知瀘州江安縣、奉職文信領兵趨之，遇害。

translations.literal: Wen Xin, magistrate of Jiang'an County in Luzhou on special assignment, led troops to rush there and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang'an magistrate Wen Xin marched to intercept them and was killed.

sentences.zh: 民皆驚擾，走保戎州。

translations.literal: The people were all alarmed and fled to take refuge in Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The populace panicked and fled to the safety of Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 轉運使寇曁咸即令諸州巡檢會江安縣，集公私船百餘艘，載糧甲，張旗幟，擊銅鑼，鼓吹，自蜀江下抵清浮壩，樹營柵，招安近界夷族，諭以大兵將至，勿與望等同惡。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Kou Xian immediately ordered the inspectors of the prefectures to assemble at Jiang'an County, gathered more than one hundred public and private boats, loaded grain and armor, raised banners, struck bronze gongs, and played music, descending from the Shu River to Qingfu Dam, erecting camp palisades, winning over nearby Yi tribes, and instructing them that a great army was coming and they should not share guilt with Wang and his fellows.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Kou Xian gathered inspectors at Jiang'an, mustered more than a hundred boats loaded with grain and arms, raised banners, beat gongs, and sailed down the Shu River to Qingfu Dam. He built camps, won over nearby Yi, and warned that a great army was coming—do not join Wang's rebels.

sentences.zh: 未幾，納溪、藍順州刺史史個松，生南八姓諸團，烏蠻獨廣王子界南廣溪移、悅等十一州刺史李紹安，山后高、鞏六州及江安界娑婆村首領，並來乞盟，立竹為誓門，刺貓狗雞血和酒飲之，誓同力討賊。

translations.literal: Before long, the prefects of Naxi and Lanshun, Shi Gesong; the eight surname clans of Shengnan; the Wuman princes Jie of Nanguang, Xiyi, Yue, and the eleven prefects including Li Shao'an; the six prefectures of Ga and Gong beyond the mountains; and the headmen of Suopo Village on the Jiang'an border all came to beg alliance, set up bamboo as a gate of oath, pierced cats, dogs, and chickens and mixed the blood with wine to drink, swearing to join forces against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon prefect Shi Gesong of Naxi and Lanshun, the eight Shengnan clans, Wuman princes and eleven prefects including Li Shao'an, six highland prefectures, and Jiang'an border headmen came to ally. They raised a bamboo oath-gate, mixed cat, dog, and chicken blood with wine, and swore to join the campaign against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 曁咸乃署榜，許以官軍至不殺其老幼，給賜衣幣酒食。

translations.literal: Xian then posted a proclamation promising that when government troops arrived they would not kill the old and young, and would grant clothing, silks, wine, and food.
translations.idiomatic: Xian posted a proclamation promising that government troops would spare women and children and reward those who submitted with clothing, cloth, wine, and food.

sentences.zh: 上遣內殿崇班王懷信乘傳與曁鹹等議綏撫方略，歒言鬥望等屢為寇鈔，恃寬赦不悛惡，今請發嘉、眉屯兵捕剪，以震懼之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Inner Palace Attendant Wang Huaixin by fast relay to discuss pacification strategy with Xian and the others. They reported that Dou Wang and others had repeatedly raided and plundered, relying on past leniency and not reforming their evil; they now requested dispatch of garrison troops from Jia and Mei to capture and cut them down so as to awe them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent inner attendant Wang Huaixin to consult with Xian on pacification. They reported that Dou Wang had raided repeatedly, trusting in past mercy, and asked for Jia and Mei garrison troops to crush them and restore fear.

sentences.zh: 六年九月，詔懷信為嘉、眉、戎、瀘等州水陸都巡檢使，閣門祗候康訓、符承訓為都同巡檢使，及發虎翼、神虎等兵三千餘人，令懷信與曁咸商度進討。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year, an edict made Huaixin overall land-and-water touring inspector of Jia, Mei, Rong, Lu, and other prefectures; the Gatehouse Attendants Kang Xun and Fu Chengxun were made co-touring inspectors; more than three thousand Tiger Wing and Divine Tiger troops were dispatched, and Huaixin was ordered to consult with Xian on the advance to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of 1013, the court named Huaixin overall land-and-water inspector for Jia, Mei, Rong, and Lu, with Kang Xun and Fu Chengxun as co-inspectors, and sent more than three thousand Tiger Wing and Divine Tiger troops for Huaixin and Xian to plan the campaign.

sentences.zh: 上因謂樞密使陳堯叟曰：「往時孫正辭討蠻，有虎翼小校率眾冒險者三人，朕志其姓名，今以配懷信。

translations.literal: The emperor then said to the Military Affairs Commissioner Chen Yaosou: "When Sun Zhengci campaigned against the Man, there were three Tiger Wing junior officers who led men through danger—I have kept their names in mind and now assign them to Huaixin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Military Affairs Commissioner Chen Yaosou: "When Sun Zhengci fought the Man, three Tiger Wing junior officers led men through the worst terrain. I remember their names and now assign them to Huaixin.

sentences.zh: 正辭嘗料簡鄉丁號'白艻子兵'，以其識山川險要，遂為鄉導，今亦令懷信召募。

translations.literal: Zhengci once selected local militia called 'White Taro Soldiers' because they knew the mountains and passes, and made them local guides—now Huaixin is also ordered to recruit them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengci once drafted local militia called 'White Taro Soldiers' who knew the terrain to serve as guides; Huaixin is to recruit them as well.

sentences.zh: 又使臣宋賁屢規畫溪洞事，適中機要，以賁知江安縣與懷信等議事。

translations.literal: Also, the envoy Song Ben had repeatedly planned gorge affairs and hit the crucial points; Ben was made magistrate of Jiang'an to deliberate with Huaixin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy Song Ben had repeatedly planned gorge campaigns with sound judgment; the court made him Jiang'an magistrate to advise Huaixin.

sentences.zh: 」歒乃點集昌、瀘、富順監白艻子弟得六千餘人。

translations.literal: " They then mustered more than six thousand White Taro youths from the Chang, Lu, and Fushun salt posts.
translations.idiomatic: " They mustered more than six thousand White Taro youths from the Chang, Lu, and Fushun posts.

sentences.zh: 十一月，懷信、康訓分領，緣溪入合灘，至生南界鬥滿村遇夷賊二千餘人，擊之，殺傷五百人，奪梭槍藤牌。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Huaixin and Kang Xun led separate columns along the stream into Hetan, reaching Douman Village on the Shengnan border, where they met more than two thousand Yi bandits, attacked them, killed and wounded five hundred, and seized spears and rattan shields.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Huaixin and Kang Xun advanced along the stream to Hetan and at Douman Village met more than two thousand Yi rebels. They killed or wounded five hundred and seized spears and rattan shields.

sentences.zh: 會暮，收眾保砦。

translations.literal: At dusk they gathered their forces and held a stockade.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk they withdrew to a fortified camp.

sentences.zh: 夷党三千餘人分兩道，張旗喊呼來逼砦柵，懷信出擊，皆潰散。

translations.literal: More than three thousand Yi in two columns raised banners and shouting to press the palisade; Huaixin sallied out and they all scattered in rout.
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand Yi advanced in two columns with banners and shouts against the camp; Huaixin sallied forth and routed them.

sentences.zh: 進壁娑婆，遇夷二千于羅固募村，又破之。

translations.literal: Advancing to fortify Suopo, they met two thousand Yi at Luogumu Village and defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: They fortified Suopo and at Luogumu Village defeated another two thousand Yi.

sentences.zh: 追至鬥行村上屏風山，連破四砦。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Pingfeng Mountain above Douxing Village, they successively stormed four stockades.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued to Pingfeng Mountain above Douxing Village and took four stockades in succession.

sentences.zh: 一日三戰，俘馘百餘人，奪資糧五千石、槍刀什器萬數，焚羅固募鬥引等三十餘村、庵舍三千區。

translations.literal: In one day they fought three battles, captured and beheaded more than one hundred, seized five thousand shi of provisions and tens of thousands of spears, blades, and implements, and burned more than thirty villages including Luogumu and Douyin and three thousand huts.
translations.idiomatic: In one day they fought three battles, took more than a hundred prisoners and heads, seized five thousand shi of grain and countless weapons, and burned more than thirty villages and three thousand huts.

sentences.zh: 懷信又引兵至鬥行村追擊過盧羅，射僕二百餘人，椚其欄柵千數。

translations.literal: Huaixin again led troops to Douxing Village, pursued past Luluo, shot down more than two hundred servants, and smashed more than a thousand of their palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Huaixin pursued from Douxing past Luluo, shot down more than two hundred men, and destroyed more than a thousand palisades.

sentences.zh: 分遣部下于羅個頰羅能落運等村及龍峨山掩殺，大獲戎具，斬首級及重傷投崖死者頗眾，燒舍千區及積谷累萬。

translations.literal: He detached subordinates for ambush kills at villages such as Yuluo, Geluo, Nengluoyun, and Long'e Mountain, gaining a great haul of war gear; heads cut off and the seriously wounded who threw themselves from cliffs were very numerous; they burned more than a thousand dwellings and piled grain in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Detachments ambushed villages including Yuluo, Geluo, and Nengluoyun and at Long'e Mountain, capturing much war gear, killing many who fell from cliffs, and burning a thousand dwellings and vast stores of grain.

sentences.zh: 兩路兵會於涇灘置砦，遣康訓部壕砦卒修涇灘路，以渡大軍。

translations.literal: The two columns met at Jingtan and set up a stockade; Kang Xun was sent with trench-stockade troops to repair the Jingtan road so the main army could cross.
translations.idiomatic: Both columns met at Jingtan and built a camp; Kang Xun's engineers repaired the Jingtan road for the main army's crossing.

sentences.zh: 俄為夷賊所邀，戰不利，訓顛於崖，死之。

translations.literal: Soon they were intercepted by Yi bandits; the battle went badly; Xun fell from a cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yi bandits soon ambushed them; the fight went badly, and Xun fell from a cliff to his death.

sentences.zh: 懷信引兵急擊，大敗之，追斬至涇灘。

translations.literal: Huaixin led troops in a swift attack, inflicted a great defeat, and pursued beheading as far as Jingtan.
translations.idiomatic: Huaixin counterattacked at once, routed them, and pursued to Jingtan.

sentences.zh: 懷信夾砦于晏江口，曁咸與符承訓偵知賊諜欲乘夜擊晏江，馳報懷信，即自涇灘拔砦赴之。

translations.literal: Huaixin pitched a camp flanking Yan River mouth; Xian and Fu Chengxun learned from scouts that enemy spies intended a night attack on Yan River and galloped to report Huaixin, who immediately broke camp at Jingtan and hurried there.
translations.idiomatic: Huaixin camped at Yan River mouth. Xian and Fu Chengxun learned the rebels planned a night attack and warned Huaixin, who broke camp at Jingtan and rushed to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 比至晏江北山，夷眾萬余已自東南合勢逼懷信砦，懷信彀強弩環砦射賊，曁鹹等整眾乘高策援，夷人大懼而卻，合擊破之，死傷千餘人。

translations.literal: By the time they reached the north hill of Yan River, more than ten thousand Yi from the southeast had already combined forces to press Huaixin's camp; Huaixin strung strong crossbows around the stockade to shoot the bandits; Xian and others arrayed their men on the heights to urge support; the Yi were greatly afraid and withdrew; a joint attack broke them, with more than a thousand dead and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: At Yan River's north hill more than ten thousand Yi had already converged on Huaixin's camp from the southeast. Huaixin ringed the camp with crossbows while Xian attacked from the heights. The Yi fled in terror; the combined assault killed or wounded more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，其酋鬥望三路分眾來鬥，又為官軍大敗，射殺數百人，溺江水死者莫計。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, the chieftain Dou Wang divided his followers in three columns to fight; they were again greatly defeated by government troops; several hundred were shot dead, and those drowned in the river were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1014, chieftain Dou Wang attacked in three columns and was routed again; hundreds were shot down and countless others drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 夷人震澁，詣軍首服，納牛羊、銅鼓、器械，曁鹹等依詔撫諭。

translations.literal: The Yi were awed and submitted; they came to the army to surrender, presenting cattle, sheep, bronze drums, and weapons; Xian and the others pacified them according to the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi submitted in awe, bringing cattle, sheep, bronze drums, and arms to surrender; Xian and his colleagues pacified them as the edict directed.

sentences.zh: 二月，還軍淯井，夷首鬥望及諸村首領悉赴監自陳，願貸死，永不寇盜邊境。

translations.literal: In the second month the army returned to Qijing Well; the Yi chieftain Dou Wang and the headmen of all the villages came to the post to confess themselves, begging mercy for their lives and swearing never again to raid the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the army withdrew to Qijing Well; chieftain Dou Wang and village headmen came to the post to plead for their lives and swear never to raid the border again.

sentences.zh: 因殺三牲盟誓，辭甚懇苦。

translations.literal: They then slaughtered three sacrificial animals to swear an oath, their words very earnest and bitter.
translations.idiomatic: They slaughtered three animals for an oath, speaking with desperate earnestness.

sentences.zh: 即犒以牢酒，感悅而去。

translations.literal: They were immediately rewarded with wine and provisions and departed gratified.
translations.idiomatic: The court feasted them with wine and provisions, and they left satisfied.

sentences.zh: 歒、懷信等上言夷人寧息，請置淯井監壕柵，並許近界市馬。

translations.literal: Xian, Huaixin, and the others memorialized that the Yi were at peace and requested establishment of trench palisades at Qijing Well post and permission for horse markets on the near border.
translations.idiomatic: Xian and Huaixin reported the Yi pacified and asked to build trenches at Qijing Well and allow border horse markets.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 八年，夔州路上言黔州西南密州夷族張聲進遣使進奉，為南寧州蕃落使龍漢曁堯邀奪，仇劫不已，乞降敕書安撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Kuizhou circuit reported that Zhang Shengjin of the Mi Prefecture Yi in southwestern Qian had sent envoys with tribute, but the Nanning tribal commissioner Long Hanyao had intercepted and robbed them; feuding and plunder continued unceasingly; they begged an edict to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1015, Kuizhou reported that Zhang Shengjin of Mi Prefecture had sent tribute envoys whom Nanning commissioner Long Hanyao had robbed; they asked for an edict of pacification.

sentences.zh: 天聖四年龍光凝、景祐三年龍光辨、康定元年龍光饧、慶曆五年龍以特、皇祐二年龍光澈等，繼以方物來貢獻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiansheng, Long Guangning came; in the third year of Jingyou, Long Guangbian; in the first year of Kangding, Long Guangtang; in the fifth year of Qingli, Long Yite; in the second year of Huangyou, Long Guangche, and others—each in turn presented local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Long Guangning in 1026, Long Guangbian in 1036, Long Guangtang in 1040, Long Yite in 1045, Long Guangche in 1050, and others successively brought tribute.

sentences.zh: 與以特俱至者七百十九人。

translations.literal: Those who arrived with Yite numbered seven hundred nineteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: Yite's party alone numbered seven hundred nineteen.

sentences.zh: 是年，以安遠將軍、知蕃落使龍光辨為甯遠軍大將軍，甯遠將軍知靜蠻軍節度使龍光凝、承宣武甯大將軍龍異豈並為安遠大將軍，承宣奉化大將軍龍異魯為武甯大將軍。

translations.literal: That year, the Pacifying-the-Distant General and tribal commissioner Long Guangbian was made Grand General of the Pacifying-the-Distant Army; the Pacifying-the-Distant General and commissioner of the Quiet-the-Man Army Long Guangning and the Proclaiming Martial Pacifying-the-Distant Grand General Long Yikai were both made Grand Generals Who Pacify the Distant; the Proclaiming and Cherishing Transformation Grand General Long Yilu was made Grand General of Martial Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: That year Guangbian became grand general of the Pacifying-the-Distant Army; Guangning and Yikai became grand generals who pacify the distant; Yilu became grand general of martial pacification.

sentences.zh: 至和中，龍以烈、龍異靜、首領張漢陛、王子羅以崇等皆入貢，命其首領而下九十三人為大將軍至郎將。

translations.literal: In the Zhihe era, Long Yilie, Long Yijing, the chieftain Zhang Hanbi, the prince Luo Yichong, and others all came to offer tribute; ninety-three persons from chieftains downward were appointed grand generals through commandants.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhihe, Long Yilie, Long Yijing, Zhang Hanbi, Prince Luo Yichong, and others brought tribute; ninety-three leaders received ranks from grand general to commandant.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，以烈復至。

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era, Yilie came again.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiayou, Yilie returned.

sentences.zh: 大率龍姓諸部族地遠且貧，熙寧中來見，賜以袍帶等物，刺其數於背。

translations.literal: For the most part the Long surname clans were remote and poor; when they came to court in the Xining era they were granted robes, belts, and the like, and their numbers were tattooed on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: The Long clans were remote and poor; in the Xining era visitors received robes and belts, with numbers tattooed on their backs.

sentences.zh: 又有張玉、石自品者，嘉祐中來貢，而鶼州亦遣人貢馬。

translations.literal: There were also Zhang Yu and Shi Zipin, who came to offer tribute in the Jiayou era, while Jian Prefecture also sent men to offer horses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu and Shi Zipin came in Jiayou, and Jian Prefecture also sent horse tribute.

sentences.zh: 有董氏世知保州曰仲元者，襲是州二十餘年矣，至是益州鈐轄司表其善拊蠻夷，命為本州刺史。

translations.literal: There was one of the Dong clan who for generations had governed Bao Prefecture named Zhongyuan, who had held that prefecture for more than twenty years; at this time the Yizhou frontier command reported his skill in soothing the Man and Yi, and he was appointed prefect of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongyuan of Bao Prefecture, who had ruled it for twenty years, was praised for pacifying the tribes and appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 鶼州、保州皆西南邊地也。

translations.literal: Jian Prefecture and Bao Prefecture were both southwestern frontier territories.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Bao were both southwestern frontier prefectures.

sentences.zh: 又有夷在瀘州部，亦西南邊地，所部十州：曰鞏、曰定、曰高、曰奉、曰淯、曰宋、曰納、曰晏、曰投附、曰長寧，皆夷人居之，依山險，善寇掠。

translations.literal: There were also Yi under Luzhou jurisdiction, likewise on the southwestern frontier; they governed ten prefectures: Gong, Ding, Gao, Feng, Yu, Song, Na, Yan, Toufu, and Changning—all inhabited by Yi who relied on mountain defiles and were skilled at raiding.
translations.idiomatic: Yi under Luzhou held ten mountainous prefectures—Gong, Ding, Gao, Feng, Yu, Song, Na, Yan, Toufu, and Changning—known for raiding.

sentences.zh: 淯井監者，在夷地中，朝廷置吏領之，以拊禦夷眾，或不得人，往往生事。

translations.literal: Qijing Well post stood in the midst of Yi territory; the court placed officials to govern it in order to control the Yi masses, but when the wrong men were chosen trouble often arose.
translations.idiomatic: Qijing Well lay deep in Yi country; poor officials often provoked incidents.

sentences.zh: 慶曆四年四月，夷人攻三江砦，詔秦鳳路總管司發兵千人選官馳往捕擊。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Qingli, Yi attacked Sanjiang Stockade; an edict ordered the Qinfeng circuit overall command to dispatch one thousand troops and select officers to hurry there and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: In April 1044, Yi attacked Sanjiang Stockade; Qinfeng circuit sent a thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 既而瀘州教練使、生南招安將史愛誘降夷賊鬥敖等，詔並補三班差使、殿侍、淯井監一路招安巡檢。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Luzhou drill instructor and Shengnan pacification general Shi Ai induced the Yi bandit Dou Ao and others to surrender; an edict appointed them all third-rank dispatch agents, palace attendants, and Qijing Well route pacification inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou instructor Shi Ai induced Dou Ao to surrender; the court made them inspectors along the Qijing route.

sentences.zh: 未幾，夷眾復寇三江砦，指使王用等擊走之。

translations.literal: Before long the Yi masses again raided Sanjiang Stockade; the commander Wang Yong and others attacked and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Yi raided Sanjiang again; Wang Yong drove them off.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年，三里村夷鬥還等百五十人復謀內寇。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou, one hundred fifty Yi of Sanli Village led by Dou Huan again plotted an inward raid.
translations.idiomatic: In 1057, one hundred fifty Yi of Sanli Village led by Dou Huan plotted another raid.

sentences.zh: 有黃土坎夷鬥蓋，長寧州人也，先以其事來告。

translations.literal: There was the Huangtukan Yi Dou Gai, a man of Changning Prefecture, who had first come to report the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangtukan Yi Dou Gai of Changning had warned the authorities first.

sentences.zh: 淯井監引兵趨之，捕斬七千餘級。

translations.literal: Qijing Well post led troops to rush there and captured and beheaded more than seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Qijing Well troops pursued them and took more than seven thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 鈐轄司上聞，詔賜鬥蓋錢三十萬、錦袍、銀帶。

translations.literal: The frontier command reported upward; an edict granted Dou Gai three hundred thousand cash, a brocade robe, and a silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded Dou Gai with three hundred thousand cash, a brocade robe, and a silver belt.

sentences.zh: 明年，又補鬥蓋長寧州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year, Dou Gai was further appointed prefect of Changning.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Dou Gai became prefect of Changning.

sentences.zh: 瀘州部舊領姚州廢已久，有烏蠻王子得蓋者來居其地，部族最盛，數遣人詣官，自言願得州名以長夷落。

translations.literal: The old Ya Prefecture jurisdiction of the Luzhou department had long been abolished; a Wuman prince named Degai came to dwell in its lands; his tribe was the most powerful and repeatedly sent men to the officials, declaring that he wished to obtain a prefectural name to extend his Yi following.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoned Ya Prefecture was resettled by the powerful Wuman prince Degai, who asked for an official prefectural title.

sentences.zh: 事聞，因賜號姚州，鑄印予之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the title Ya Prefecture was granted and a seal cast and given to him.
translations.idiomatic: The court restored the name Ya Prefecture and cast a seal for him.

sentences.zh: 得蓋又乞敕書一通以遺子孫，詔從其請。

translations.literal: Degai also requested one imperial edict to leave to his descendants; an edict granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Degai also asked for an edict to pass to his heirs, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 夔州路又有溱、南二州夷，頗盛強，皇祐初，詔自今歲遣使者存問之。

translations.literal: On the Kuizhou circuit there were also the Qin and Nan prefecture Yi, quite powerful; at the beginning of Huangyou an edict ordered that from this year envoys should be sent to inquire after them.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin and Nan Yi of Kuizhou were powerful; in 1049 the court ordered annual envoys to visit them.

sentences.zh: 雅州西山野川路蠻者，亦西南夷之別種也，距州三百里，有部落四十六，唐以來皆為羈縻州。

translations.literal: The Yechuan Road Man of western Ya Prefecture were also a separate branch of the southwestern Yi, three hundred li from the prefecture, with forty-six tribes; since the Tang they had all been jimi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The Yechuan Road Man west of Ya were a southwestern Yi branch three hundred li away, with forty-six jimi tribes since Tang times.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，首領馬令膜等十四人以名馬、犎牛、虎豹皮、麝臍來貢，並上唐朝敕書告身凡七通，咸賜以冠帶，其首領悉授官以遣之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo, the chieftain Ma Lingmo and fourteen others came to offer fine horses, zebu cattle, tiger and leopard skins, and musk, and also presented seven Tang edicts and commissions; all were granted caps and belts, and the chieftains were all given offices and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: In 978, chieftain Ma Lingmo and fourteen others brought horses, cattle, pelts, and musk, presenting seven Tang commissions; all received caps, belts, and offices.

sentences.zh: 紹聖二年，以碉門砦蠻部王元壽襲懷化司戈云。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaosheng, Wang Yuanshou of the Diaomen Stockade Man tribe succeeded to the post of Marshal Who Cherishes Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1095, Wang Yuanshou of Diaomen Stockade succeeded as marshal who cherishes transformation.

sentences.zh: 黎州諸蠻，凡十二種：曰山后兩林蠻，在州南七日程；

translations.literal: Among the Man of Lizhou there are twelve kinds: the Shanhou Lianglin Man, seven days' journey south of the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: The Lizhou tribes comprise twelve groups, beginning with the Shanhou Lianglin Man seven days south of the prefecture;

sentences.zh: 曰邛部川蠻，在州東南十二程；

translations.literal: the Qiongbu River Man, twelve stages southeast of the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: the Qiongbu River Man twelve stages to the southeast;

sentences.zh: 曰風琶蠻，在州西南一千一百里；

translations.literal: the Fengpa Man, eleven hundred li southwest of the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: the Fengpa Man eleven hundred li southwest;

sentences.zh: 曰保塞蠻，在州西南三百里；

translations.literal: the Baosai Man, three hundred li southwest of the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: the Baosai Man three hundred li southwest;

sentences.zh: 曰三王蠻，亦曰部落蠻，在州西百里；

translations.literal: the Sanwang Man, also called the Tribal Man, one hundred li west of the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: the Sanwang or Tribal Man one hundred li west;

sentences.zh: 曰西箐蠻，有彌羌部落，在州西三百里；

translations.literal: the Xiqing Man, with the Miqang tribe, three hundred li west of the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: the Xiqing Man with the Miqang tribe three hundred li west;

sentences.zh: 曰淨浪蠻，在州南一百五十里；

translations.literal: the Jinglang Man, one hundred fifty li south of the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: the Jinglang Man one hundred fifty li south;

sentences.zh: 曰白蠻，在州東南一百里；

translations.literal: the Bai Man, one hundred li southeast of the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: the Bai Man one hundred li southeast;

sentences.zh: 曰烏蒙蠻，在州東南千里；

translations.literal: the Wumeng Man, one thousand li southeast of the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: the Wumeng Man a thousand li southeast;

sentences.zh: 曰阿宗蠻，在州西南二日程。

translations.literal: the Azong Man, two days' journey southwest of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: the Azong Man two days southwest.

sentences.zh: 凡風琶、兩林、邛部皆謂之東蠻，其餘小蠻各分隸焉。

translations.literal: Fengpa, Lianglin, and Qiongbu are all called Eastern Man; the remaining small tribes are each subordinate in division.
translations.idiomatic: Fengpa, Lianglin, and Qiongbu were Eastern Man; smaller tribes fell under them.

sentences.zh: 邛部于諸蠻中最驕悍狡譎，招集蕃漢亡命，侵攘他種，閉其道以專利。

translations.literal: Among all the tribes Qiongbu was the most arrogant, fierce, and cunning, gathering fugitives from among the Fan and Han, encroaching on and plundering other tribes, and closing the roads to monopolize profit.
translations.idiomatic: Qiongbu was the proudest and most treacherous, sheltering fugitives, raiding neighbors, and monopolizing the trade routes.

sentences.zh: 曰大雲南蠻，曰小雲南蠻，即唐南詔，今名大理國，自有傳。

translations.literal: There are the Great Yunnan Man and the Small Yunnan Man—that is, the Tang's Nanzhao, now called the Dali state, which has its own separate account.
translations.idiomatic: Great and Small Yunnan Man were Tang Nanzhao, now Dali, which has its own account.

sentences.zh: 夷俗尚鬼，謂主祭者鬼主，故其酋長號都鬼主。

translations.literal: Yi custom reveres ghosts; the chief sacrificer is called the Ghost Master, and therefore their chieftains are titled Chief Ghost Master of the Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi revered ghosts; their chief sacrificer was the Ghost Master, and chieftains were called Chief Ghost Masters.

sentences.zh: 山后兩林蠻，後唐天成間始來貢。

translations.literal: The Shanhou Lianglin Man first came to offer tribute in the Later Tang Tiancheng era.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanhou Lianglin Man first sent tribute in the Later Tang Tiancheng era.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年六月壬子，勿兒遣部落將軍離魚以狀白黎州，期十月內入貢，成都府以聞，詔嘉答之。

translations.literal: On the sixth month, renyin day of the second year of Kaibao, Wuer sent the tribal general Liyu to notify Lizhou in a memorial that he would enter to offer tribute within the tenth month; Chengdu Prefecture reported it, and an edict praised and answered him.
translations.idiomatic: In June 969, Wuer notified Lizhou that he would tribute by the tenth month; Chengdu reported it and the court responded warmly.

sentences.zh: 至是來朝，賜以器幣。

translations.literal: On this occasion he came to court and was granted vessels and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He now came to court and received vessels and silks.

sentences.zh: 由黎州南行七日而至其地，又一程，至溋州。

translations.literal: From Lizhou southward seven days reaches their territory; one more stage reaches Wen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days south from Lizhou lay their lands; one more stage reached Wen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 溋州今廢，空城中但有浮圖一。

translations.literal: Wen Prefecture is now abolished; in the empty city there is only one pagoda.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Prefecture was abandoned; only a pagoda remained in the empty city.

sentences.zh: 又二程，至建昌城。

translations.literal: Two more stages reach Jiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Two stages farther lay Jiancheng.

sentences.zh: 又十七程，至雲南。

translations.literal: Seventeen more stages reach Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen stages beyond that lay Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，又朝貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year they again came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year they tribute again.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，邛部川歸德將軍阿伏上言，為山后兩蠻勿兒率眾侵掠堡砦。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year, the General Who Returns to Virtue of Qiongbu River, Afu, memorialized that Wuer of the two Lianglin tribes beyond the mountains was leading a crowd to invade and plunder stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In 971, Afu of Qiongbu reported that Wuer of the two Lianglin tribes was raiding stockades.

sentences.zh: 八年，懷化將軍勿尼等六十余人來貢，詔以勿尼為歸德將軍，又以兩林蠻大鬼主蘇吠為懷化將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Cherishing Transformation General Wuni and more than sixty others came to offer tribute; an edict made Wuni General Who Returns to Virtue and the Great Ghost Master of the two Lianglin tribes, Su Fei, General Who Cherishes Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: In 975, Wuni and sixty others came to court; Wuni became General Who Returns to Virtue and Su Fei General Who Cherishes Transformation.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，遣使王子卑彩、副使牟蓋、鬼主還祖等七十八人以名馬來貢，乞頒正朔。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, the envoy Prince Beicai, Vice Envoy Mougai, Ghost Master Huizu, and seventy-eight others came with fine horses as tribute and begged issuance of the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: In 977, Prince Beicai, Mougai, Huizu, and seventy-eight others brought horses and asked for the calendar.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「山后兩林要蠻主歸德將軍勿尼、懷化將軍勿兒等克慕聲明，遠修職貢，並增環衛之秩，俾為夷落之榮。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The chieftains of the Shanhou Lianglin Yao Man, General Who Returns to Virtue Wuni, General Who Cherishes Transformation Wuer, and others admire our renown and have come from afar to fulfill tribute duties—all are promoted in court rank to be the glory of the Yi tribes."
translations.idiomatic: The edict praised Wuni and Wuer for distant tribute and promised higher rank.

sentences.zh: 勿尼可特授歸德大將軍，勿兒可特授懷化大將軍。

translations.literal: Wuni may be specially appointed Grand General Who Returns to Virtue; Wuer may be specially appointed Grand General Who Cherishes Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Wuni became Grand General Who Returns to Virtue; Wuer became Grand General Who Cherishes Transformation.

sentences.zh: 」是冬，又遣使離魚貢犀二株、馬九匹，來賀登極。

translations.literal: " That winter they again sent the envoy Liyu to offer two rhinoceros horns and nine horses to congratulate the accession.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Liyu brought two rhinoceros horns and nine horses to congratulate the accession.

sentences.zh: 四年，勿兒與都鬼主又遣王子祚遇以名馬來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Wuer and the Chief Ghost Master again sent Prince Zuoyu with fine horses as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 979, Wuer sent Prince Zuoyu with fine horses.

sentences.zh: 八年，蠻主弟牟昂及王子牟蓋、摩忙、卑愧、副使牟計等二百三十九人來貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the chieftain's younger brother Mouang and the princes Mougai, Momang, Beikui, Vice Envoy Mouji, and two hundred thirty-nine others came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 983, Mouang, Mougai, and two hundred thirty-nine others came to court.

sentences.zh: 詔以牟昂為懷化大將軍，牟蓋等三人為歸德郎將，牟計等百二十人並為懷化司戈。

translations.literal: An edict made Mouang Grand General Who Cherishes Transformation, the three men Mougai and others Commandants Who Return to Virtue, and Mouji and one hundred twenty others Marshals Who Cherish Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Mouang became grand general; Mougai and others became commandants; Mouji and one hundred twenty became marshals.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，勿尼等及其王子李奉恩復來貢馬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, Wuni and his prince Li Fengen again came to offer horses as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 986, Wuni and Prince Li Fengen brought horses again.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，王子離魚、副使卑都、卑諭、鬼主曵皮禮等百二十八人來貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua, Prince Liyu, Vice Envoys Beidu, Beiyu, Ghost Master Yipili, and one hundred twenty-eight others came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 990, Liyu, Beidu, Yipili, and one hundred twenty-eight others came to court.

sentences.zh: 詔授離魚歸德將軍，卑都保順郎將，卑諭歸德司戈，卑熱等五十四人懷化司戈。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Liyu General Who Returns to Virtue, Beidu Commandant Who Protects and Submits, Beiyu Marshal of Returning Virtue, and Beire and fifty-four others Marshals Who Cherish Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Liyu became general; Beidu commandant; Beiyu marshal; fifty-four others became marshals.

sentences.zh: 天禧二年，山后兩林百蠻都鬼主李阿善遣將軍卑熱等一百五十人來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxi, the Chief Ghost Master of the Shanhou Lianglin Hundred Tribes, Li Ashan, sent the general Beire and one hundred fifty others to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 1018, Chief Ghost Master Li Ashan sent Beire and one hundred fifty men with tribute.

sentences.zh: 邛部川蠻，亦曰大路蠻，亦曰勿鄧，居漢越溋郡會無縣地。

translations.literal: The Qiongbu River Man are also called the Great Road Man, also called Wudeng; they dwell in the territory of Huiwu County of the Han Yuewen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiongbu River Man, also called Great Road or Wudeng Man, lived in ancient Yuewen's Huiwu County.

sentences.zh: 其酋長自稱「百蠻都鬼主」。

translations.literal: Their chieftain styles himself "Chief Ghost Master of the Hundred Tribes."
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftain called himself Chief Ghost Master of the Hundred Tribes.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年六月，都鬼主阿伏白黎州，期以十月令王子入貢，成都府以聞，詔嘉納之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Kaibao, Chief Ghost Master Afu notified Lizhou that in the tenth month he would send princes to offer tribute; Chengdu Prefecture reported it, and an edict praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: In June 969, Afu promised tribute by the tenth month; the court welcomed it.

sentences.zh: 四年，黎州定遠兵士構叛，聚居鹿角溪，阿伏令弟遊擊將軍卑吠等率眾平之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Lizhou Dingyuan soldiers mutinied and gathered at Lujiao Stream; Afu ordered his younger brother, Strike General Beifei, to lead a crowd and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In 971, mutinous Lizhou troops gathered at Lujiao Stream; Afu's brother Beifei suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 詔賜阿伏銀帶、錦袍，並賜其眾銀帛各百，以為歸德將軍。

translations.literal: An edict granted Afu a silver belt and brocade robe, and also granted his followers one hundred pieces of silver and silk each, making him General Who Returns to Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave Afu a silver belt and brocade robe, rewarded his men, and named him General Who Returns to Virtue.

sentences.zh: 六年，阿伏與山后兩林蠻主勿兒言語相失，勿兒率兵侵邛部川，頗俘殺部落。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Afu and the Lianglin chieftain Wuer had a falling-out in speech; Wuer led troops to invade Qiongbu River and captured and killed many of the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In 973, Afu quarreled with Wuer, who invaded Qiongbu and killed many tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 黎州以聞，並賜詔慰諭，令各守封疆，勿相侵犯。

translations.literal: Lizhou reported it; edicts of comfort and instruction were granted to both, ordering each to keep to his borders and not invade one another.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhou reported the feud; both received edicts ordering them to keep the peace.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，首領牟昂、諸族鬼主副使離襪等各以方物來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, the chieftain Mouang, the tribal Ghost Master Vice Envoy Liwu, and others each came with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 979, Mouang, Liwu, and others brought local goods.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，都鬼主諾驅並其母熱免遣王子阿有等百七十二人以方物、名馬來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, Chief Ghost Master Nuoqu and his mother Remian sent Prince Ayuo and one hundred seventy-two others with local products and fine horses as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 985, Nuoqu and his mother Remian sent Prince Ayuo with one hundred seventy-two men.

sentences.zh: 詔以諾驅為懷化將軍，並賜其母銀器。

translations.literal: An edict made Nuoqu General Who Cherishes Transformation and also granted his mother silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Nuoqu became General Who Cherishes Transformation; his mother received silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，遣弟少蓋等三百五十人來賀籍田，貢禦馬十四匹、馬二百八十匹、犀角二、象牙二、莎羅毯一、合金銀飾蠻刀二、金飾馬鞍勒一具、敎原羊十、撐牛六。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong, he sent his younger brother Shaogai and three hundred fifty others to congratulate the plowing ceremony, offering fourteen imperial horses, two hundred eighty horses, two rhinoceros horns, two elephant tusks, one shaluo rug, two alloy silver-decorated Man blades, one gold-decorated saddle and bridle set, ten jiaoyuan sheep, and six zebu cattle.
translations.idiomatic: In 989, Shaogai and three hundred fifty others congratulated the plowing rite with horses, horns, ivory, rugs, blades, saddles, sheep, and zebu.

sentences.zh: 詔以少蓋為歸德郎將。

translations.literal: An edict made Shaogai Commandant Who Returns to Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Shaogai became Commandant Who Returns to Virtue.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，諾驅自部馬二百五十匹至黎州求互市，詔增給其直。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua, Nuoqu brought two hundred fifty horses from his tribe to Lizhou seeking mutual trade; an edict increased the payment given.
translations.idiomatic: In 990, Nuoqu brought two hundred fifty horses to Lizhou to trade; the court raised the price.

sentences.zh: 諾驅令譯者言更入西蕃求良馬以中市。

translations.literal: Nuoqu had an interpreter say he would enter the western Fan lands to seek fine horses to bring to the market.
translations.idiomatic: Nuoqu said through an interpreter that he would seek better horses in the western Fan lands.

sentences.zh: 二年，復遣子牟昂、叔離襪以方物、良馬、嫠牛來貢，仍乞加恩。

translations.literal: In the second year, he again sent his son Mouang and his uncle Liwu with local products, fine horses, and zebu cattle as tribute, still begging added favor.
translations.idiomatic: In 991, Mouang and Liwu returned with goods, horses, and zebu, asking for favor.

sentences.zh: 詔授諾驅懷化大將軍，少蓋懷化將軍，牟昂歸德將軍，離襪懷化司戈；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Nuoqu Grand General Who Cherishes Transformation, Shaogai General Who Cherishes Transformation, Mouang General Who Returns to Virtue, and Liwu Marshal Who Cherishes Transformation;
translations.idiomatic: Nuoqu became grand general; Shaogai general; Mouang general who returns to virtue; Liwu marshal.

sentences.zh: 又封諾驅母歸德郡太君熱免甯遠郡太君，弟離遮、小男阿醉都判官，任彥德等一百九十一人為懷化司戈。

translations.literal: also enfeoffed Nuoqu's mother, the Lady of Returning Virtue Commandery Remian, as Lady of Pacifying-the-Distant Commandery; his younger brother Lizhe, his young son Azui, and the adjutants, and Ren Yande and one hundred ninety-one others were made Marshals Who Cherish Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Nuoqu's mother Remian became Lady of Pacifying-the-Distant Commandery; one hundred ninety-one followers became marshals.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，李順亂西川，王繼恩討平之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, Li Shun rebelled in western Sichuan; Wang Jien pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In 995, Li Shun rebelled in western Sichuan and Wang Jien suppressed him.

sentences.zh: 遣嘉州牙校辛顯使，諾驅奉淳化二年所授官告、敕書及日曆為信，因言與賊樊秀等接戰，敗之，復請朝覲，通嘉州舊路。

translations.literal: He sent the Jia Prefecture military adjutant Xin Xian as envoy; Nuoqu presented the commission and edict granted in the second year of Chunhua and the calendar as credentials, stating that he had joined battle with the bandits Fan Xiu and others, defeated them, and again requested an audience and reopening of the old Jia Prefecture road.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Xin Xian visited Nuoqu, who presented his Chunhua commissions and reported defeating Fan Xiu, asking to reopen the Jia road.

sentences.zh: 繼恩上言：「通嘉州路非便，只令于黎州賣馬。

translations.literal: Jien memorialized: "Opening the Jia Prefecture road is not convenient; let them sell horses only at Lizhou."
translations.idiomatic: Jien argued the Jia road was inconvenient and said they should sell horses only at Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 」詔不允。

translations.literal: " An edict did not grant this.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused.

sentences.zh: 其入覲王子一十九人並加官，鬼主三十六人並賜敕書以撫之。

translations.literal: The nineteen princes who came to court were all promoted in office, and thirty-six Ghost Masters were all granted edicts to soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen princes were promoted and thirty-six Ghost Masters received soothing edicts.

sentences.zh: 至道三年，遣王子阿醉來朝。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhidao, he sent Prince Azui to court.
translations.idiomatic: In 997, he sent Prince Azui to court.

sentences.zh: 真宗咸平二年，遣王子部的等來貢文犀、名馬，賜衣帶、器幣有差。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping of Emperor Zhenzong, he sent Prince Budi and others to offer patterned rhinoceros and fine horses; robes, belts, vessels, and silks were granted in differing measure.
translations.idiomatic: In 999, Prince Budi brought rhinoceros and horses and received graded gifts.

sentences.zh: 又乞給印，以「大渡河南山前、後都鬼主」為文，從之。

translations.literal: He also begged issuance of a seal with the inscription "Chief Ghost Master before and behind the mountains south of the Dadu River"; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He also received a seal reading Chief Ghost Master before and behind the mountains south of the Dadu River.

sentences.zh: 五年，又遣王子離歸等二百余人入貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he again sent Prince Ligui and more than two hundred others to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 1002, Prince Ligui and more than two hundred others came to court.

sentences.zh: 六年，黎州言邛部川都蠻王諾驅卒，其子阿遒立。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Lizhou reported that the Qiongbu River Chief Man King Nuoqu had died and his son Aqiu had succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In 1003, Lizhou reported Nuoqu's death and his son Aqiu's succession.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，阿遒遣王子將軍百九十二人來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, Aqiu sent one hundred ninety-two princes and generals to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 1005, Aqiu sent one hundred ninety-two princes and generals.

sentences.zh: 詔授阿遒安遠將軍，阿遒叔懷化將軍，阿育為歸德將軍，離歸為懷化將軍，大判官懷化司候任彥德、王子將軍部的並為懷化郎將，判官任惟慶為懷化司候。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Aqiu General Who Pacifies the Distant, Aqiu's uncle General Who Cherishes Transformation, Ayu General Who Returns to Virtue, Ligui General Who Cherishes Transformation, the great adjutant and Marshal Who Cherishes Transformation Registrar Ren Yande and Prince-General Budi both Commandants Who Cherish Transformation, and Adjutant Ren Weiqing Marshal Who Cherishes Transformation Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Aqiu became General Who Pacifies the Distant; his uncle, Ayu, Ligui, Ren Yande, Budi, and Ren Weiqing received ranks.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，遣將軍趙勿娑等獻名馬、犀角、象齒、娑羅毯，會于泰山。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he sent General Zhao Wusuo and others to present fine horses, rhinoceros horns, elephant ivory, and shaluo rugs, meeting at Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In 1008, Zhao Wusuo and others brought horses, horns, ivory, and rugs to Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，阿遒加恩。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, Aqiu received added favor.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites, Aqiu received added favor.

sentences.zh: 勿娑等厚賜遣還。

translations.literal: Wusuo and the others were richly rewarded and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Wusuo and his party were richly rewarded and sent home.

sentences.zh: 天聖八年十月，邛部川都蠻王黎在遣卑郎、離滅等來貢方物。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year of Tiansheng, the Qiongbu River Chief Man King Lizai sent Beilang, Limie, and others to offer local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In October 1030, Chief Man King Lizai of Qiongbu sent Beilang and Limie with tribute.

sentences.zh: 時占城、龜茲、沙州亦皆入貢，至以家自隨。

translations.literal: At the time Champa, Kucha, and Shazhou also all came to offer tribute, even bringing their families with them.
translations.idiomatic: Champa, Kucha, and Shazhou also sent tribute, some even bringing their families.

sentences.zh: 晏殊因請圖其人物衣冠，並訪道裏風俗以上史官，詔可。

translations.literal: Yan Shu therefore requested portraits of their persons and dress and inquiry into routes and customs for the historiographers; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shu asked that their dress be painted and their routes and customs recorded for the historians; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，命黎在為保義將軍，又命其部族為郎將、司戈、司候，凡三十餘人。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year, Lizai was appointed General Who Protects Righteousness, and more than thirty of his tribesmen were appointed commandants, marshals, and registrars.
translations.idiomatic: In March 1031, Lizai became General Who Protects Righteousness; more than thirty followers received offices.

sentences.zh: 明道元年，黎州言黎在請三歲一貢，詔諭以道路遐遠，聽五年一至。

translations.literal: In the first year of Mingdao, Lizhou reported that Lizai requested tribute every three years; an edict explained the great distance and allowed one visit every five years.
translations.idiomatic: In 1032, Lizai asked to tribute every three years; the court allowed every five because of the distance.

sentences.zh: 景祐初，黎州復言邛部蠻請歲入貢，詔如明道令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyou, Lizhou again reported that the Qiongbu Man requested annual tribute; an edict followed the Mingdao rule.
translations.idiomatic: In 1034, annual tribute was again requested; the court repeated the five-year rule.

sentences.zh: 寶元元年，百蠻都王忙海遣將軍卑蓋等貢方物，且請三歲一貢，不許。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoyuan, the Hundred Tribes King Manghai sent General Beigai and others with local products and also requested tribute every three years; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1038, King Manghai sent Beigai with goods and asked for triennial tribute; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 慶曆四年，邛部川山前、山后百蠻都鬼主牟黑遣將軍阿濟等三百三十九人獻馬二百一十、嫠牛一、大角羊四、犀株一、莎羅毯一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qingli, the Chief Ghost Master before and behind the mountains of Qiongbu River, Mouhei, sent General Aji and three hundred thirty-nine others presenting two hundred ten horses, one zebu, four great-horned sheep, one rhinoceros horn, and one shaluo rug.
translations.idiomatic: In 1044, Mouhei sent Aji with three hundred thirty-nine men, two hundred ten horses, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 慶曆間，有都鬼主弁黑等入貢。

translations.literal: During the Qingli era, Chief Ghost Masters such as Bianhei came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingli, Chief Ghost Master Bianhei and others tribute.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其王咩墨擾邊，知黎州孫固使其首領苴克殺之。

translations.literal: Before long their king Miemo harassed the border; Lizhou prefect Sun Gu had his chieftain Juke kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon King Miemo raided the border; prefect Sun Gu had chieftain Juke kill him.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，苴克遣使來賀登寶位，自稱「大渡河南邛部川山前、山后百蠻都首領」，賜敕書、器幣、襲衣、銀帶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, Juke sent envoys to congratulate the accession, styling himself "Chief of the Hundred Tribes before and behind the mountains south of the Dadu River in Qiongbu River," and was granted an edict, vessels, silks, court dress, and a silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: In 1070, Juke congratulated the accession as chief south of the Dadu and received an edict, gifts, court dress, and a silver belt.

sentences.zh: 是年，苴克死，詔以其子韋則為懷化校尉、大渡河南邛部川都鬼主。

translations.literal: That year Juke died; an edict made his son Weize Pacification Cadet and Chief Ghost Master of Qiongbu south of the Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: That year Juke died; his son Weize succeeded as cadet and chief ghost master.

sentences.zh: 九年，遣其將軍卑郎等十四人入貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he sent his general Beilang and fourteen others to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 1076, he sent General Beilang and fourteen others with tribute.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，詔以崖鹁蔑襲兄蒙備金紫光祿大夫、懷化校尉、都鬼主如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao, an edict made Yan Bomei succeed his elder brother Mengbei as Grand Master of the Golden Purple Glory Light, Pacification Cadet, and Chief Ghost Master as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 1165, Yan Bomei succeeded his brother Mengbei with the same ranks.

sentences.zh: 淳熙元年，吐蕃寇西邊，崖鹁蔑率眾掩擊，詔嘉其功。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunxi, Tibetans raided the western border; Yan Bomei led a force in a surprise attack; an edict praised his merit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1174, Yan Bomei ambushed Tibetan raiders and was praised.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，兩林蠻王弟籠畏及酋長崖來率部義等攻邛部川之籠甕城，不克，大掠而去。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year, the Lianglin king's younger brother Longwei and the chieftain Yailai led Buyi and others to attack Longweng city of Qiongbu River, failed to take it, and plundered greatly as they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In May 1175, Longwei and Yailai attacked Longweng city, failed, and looted as they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 崖鹁蔑追之，不及。

translations.literal: Yan Bomei pursued but did not overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bomei pursued but could not catch them.

sentences.zh: 制置使范成大檄黎州嚴加備禦。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Fan Chengda ordered Lizhou to strengthen defenses strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chengda ordered Lizhou to strengthen its defenses.

sentences.zh: 八年，崖鹁蔑死，其侄墨崖襲職。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Yan Bomei died; his nephew Moyai succeeded to the post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1181, Yan Bomei died; his nephew Moyai succeeded.

sentences.zh: 詔黎州屯戍土軍、禁軍及西兵，遇有邊事並聽本州守臣節制。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Lizhou's local garrison, forbidden troops, and western troops, when border affairs arose, all obey the prefectural commander.
translations.idiomatic: Border troops at Lizhou were placed under the prefect's command.

sentences.zh: 嘉定九年，邛部川逼于雲南，遂伏屬之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiading, Qiongbu River, pressed by Yunnan, submitted to it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1216, Qiongbu submitted to Yunnan under pressure.

sentences.zh: 其族素效順，捍禦邊陲，既折歸雲南，失西南一藩籬矣。

translations.literal: That clan had long been obedient and defended the frontier; once they bent to Yunnan, the southwest lost a screen.
translations.idiomatic: A loyal frontier clan was lost to Yunnan, weakening the southwest.

sentences.zh: 風琶蠻，咸平初，其王曩䓾䓾遣使烏柏等貢馬五十七匹，素地紅花娑羅毯二，來賀即位。

translations.literal: The Fengpa Man: at the beginning of Xianping, their king Nangzhezhe sent Wubai and others with fifty-seven horses and two plain-ground red-flower shaluo rugs to congratulate the accession.
translations.idiomatic: In 998, King Nangzhezhe sent Wubai with horses and rugs to congratulate the accession.

sentences.zh: 詔授曩䓾及進奉使等官，優賜遣之。
