translations.literal: An edict granted Nangzhe and the tribute envoys offices and sent them away with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted offices and generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，又遣烏柏來貢，詔授曩䓾歸德將軍，烏柏等四十六人弟遷郎將、司階、司戈。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde, Wubai came again; an edict made Nangzhe General Who Returns to Virtue and forty-six others including Wubai commandants, registrars, or marshals.
translations.idiomatic: In 1006, Wubai returned; Nangzhe became general and forty-six followers received ranks.

sentences.zh: 保塞蠻，開寶間，其蠻七十餘人由大渡河來歸，時時來貨其善馬。

translations.literal: The Baosai Man: in the Kaibao era, more than seventy of their tribesmen came to submit by the Dadu River and from time to time came to sell their fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaibao era, seventy Baosai tribesmen submitted and traded horses.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十七年，川、秦都大司言：「漢地民張太二姑率眾劫殺市馬蠻客崖遇等，恐啟邊釁，已加慰諭，並償其直矣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Shaoxing, the Sichuan-Qin frontier commissioner reported: "Han subject Zhang Tai'ergu led a crowd to rob and kill the horse-trading Man guest Yaiyu and others; fearing border trouble, they have already been comforted and compensated.
translations.idiomatic: In 1157, Zhang Tai'ergu robbed Man horse traders; officials compensated them to avoid trouble.

sentences.zh: 」詔免知州唐栾及通判陳伯強官，抵首賊法。

translations.literal: " An edict stripped Prefect Tang Luan and Vice Prefect Chen Boqiang of office and punished the chief bandits by law.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect and vice prefect were dismissed and the ringleaders punished.

sentences.zh: 部落蠻，有劉、楊、郝、趙、王五姓。

translations.literal: The Tribal Man had five surnames: Liu, Yang, Hao, Zhao, and Wang.
translations.idiomatic: The Tribal Man had Liu, Yang, Hao, Zhao, and Wang clans.

sentences.zh: 淳熙七年十月，黎州五部落蠻貢馬三百匹求內附，詔許通互市，卻其所獻馬。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year of Chunxi, the five tribal Man of Lizhou offered three hundred horses seeking inner attachment; an edict permitted mutual markets and returned the horses presented.
translations.idiomatic: In 1180, five tribes offered three hundred horses seeking attachment; the court allowed trade and returned the horses.

sentences.zh: 彌羌部落。

translations.literal: The Miqang tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The Miqang tribe.

sentences.zh: 乾道九年，吐蕃青羌以知黎州宇文紹直不仇其馬價，憤怨為亂。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qiandao, the Qingyi of Tibet rebelled because Lizhou prefect Yu Wen Shaozhi would not pay their horse prices fairly.
translations.idiomatic: In 1173, Qingyi Tibetans rebelled over unfair horse prices at Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 詔帥憲撫安之，紹直罷免。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the circuit and judicial commissioners to pacify them; Shaozhi was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were ordered to pacify them; Shaozhi was removed.

sentences.zh: 青羌首領奴兒結等市馬黎州，大肆虜掠，權州事王窭多給金帛，亟遣還。

translations.literal: The Qingyi chieftain Nuerjie and others traded horses at Lizhou and plundered greatly; the acting prefect Wang Ju gave much gold and silk and quickly sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Nuerjie traded at Lizhou but raided; Wang Ju bribed them to leave.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使虞允文言窭貪功，恐他部效尤，漸啟邊釁。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Yu Yunwen said Ju sought merit greedily and feared others would imitate him, gradually opening border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen warned that Wang Ju's greed would invite wider trouble.

sentences.zh: 詔降窭兩官。

translations.literal: An edict reduced Ju two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 十月，黎州吐蕃復寇邊，攻虎掌砦。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Lizhou Tibetans again raided the border and attacked Huzhang Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Tibetans attacked Huzhang Stockade.

sentences.zh: 詔四川宣撫司檄成都府調兵二千人戍黎州以禦之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Sichuan pacification office to instruct Chengdu to dispatch two thousand troops to garrison Lizhou to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu sent two thousand troops to garrison Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，奴兒結還所虜生口三十九人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunxi, Nuerjie returned thirty-nine captives.
translations.idiomatic: In 1175, Nuerjie returned thirty-nine captives.

sentences.zh: 黎州與之盟，復聽其互市，給賞歸之。

translations.literal: Lizhou made a treaty with them, again allowed mutual trade, gave rewards, and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhou made peace, reopened trade, rewarded them, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 制置使范成大言：「所虜未盡歸我，豈可復與通好？

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Fan Chengda said: "The captives have not all been returned to us—how can we be friendly again?
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chengda objected: "Not all captives are returned—how can we make peace?

sentences.zh: 」詔謫宇文紹直，編管千里外。

translations.literal: " An edict banished Yu Wen Shaozhi to registered exile a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhi was exiled a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 成大增黎州五砦，籍強壯五千人為戰兵；

translations.literal: Chengda added five stockades at Lizhou and registered five thousand strong men as battle troops;
translations.idiomatic: Chengda added five stockades and five thousand militia;

sentences.zh: 吐蕃入寇之徑凡十有八，皆築堡戍之。

translations.literal: there were eighteen routes by which Tibetans entered to raid—all were fortified with forts.
translations.idiomatic: eighteen Tibetan invasion routes were fortified.

sentences.zh: 奴兒結率眾二千扣安靜砦。

translations.literal: Nuerjie led two thousand men to press Anjing Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Nuerjie besieged Anjing with two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 成大調飛山卒千人赴之，度其三日必遁，戒勿追。

translations.literal: Chengda dispatched a thousand Feishan troops; estimating they would flee within three days, he warned against pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Chengda sent a thousand troops and ordered no pursuit after three days.

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: Soon it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: They fled as he predicted.

sentences.zh: 青羌奴兒結為邊害者十餘年，其後制置使留正以計禽殺之，盡殲其黨。

translations.literal: The Qingyi Nuerjie had been a border harm for more than ten years; later Pacification Commissioner Liu Zheng captured and killed him and exterminated his faction.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years, Liu Zheng captured and killed Nuerjie and destroyed his faction.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十二年，趙汝愚代為制置使，或謂殺降不祥，必啟邊患，汝愚不為動，但分守險要，嚴備以待之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chunxi, Zhao Ruoyu replaced him as pacification commissioner; some said killing those who surrendered was ill-omened and would open border trouble, but Ruoyu was unmoved and only divided forces to hold defiles and waited in strict readiness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1185, Zhao Ruoyu ignored warnings that killing surrendering tribes would bring trouble and held the passes.

sentences.zh: 明年，奴兒結弟三開果入寇，邊備完固，三開不能攻，走歸。

translations.literal: The next year Nuerjie's younger brother Sankai indeed raided; the border defenses were complete and Sankai could not attack and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Sankai raided but could not break the defenses and fled.

sentences.zh: 汝愚縣重賞以間群蠻，三開不能孤立，遂以憂死。

translations.literal: Ruoyu posted heavy rewards to sow discord among the tribes; Sankai could not stand alone and died of anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoyu bribed discord among the tribes; Sankai died isolated.

sentences.zh: 時虛恨蠻族最強，破小路蠻，並其地，與黎州接壤，請通互市。

translations.literal: At the time the Xuhen Man tribe was strongest; they destroyed the Xiaolu Man and annexed their lands, bordering Lizhou, and requested mutual trade.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuhen tribe, strongest in the region, annexed neighbors and sought trade with Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 汝愚以黎州三面被邊，若更通虛恨蠻，恐重貽他日之憂，不若拒之為便。

translations.literal: Ruoyu said Lizhou was bordered on three sides; if Xuhen were also allowed trade, he feared adding future trouble—it was better to refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoyu refused Xuhen trade lest Lizhou face another threat.

sentences.zh: 帝以其知大體，從之。

translations.literal: The emperor, deeming him to know the larger pattern, followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his judgment.

sentences.zh: 尋汝愚以定青羌功加龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: Soon Ruoyu was promoted to Hanlin Academician for pacifying the Qingyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoyu was promoted for pacifying the Qingyi.

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年十二月，彌羌蓄卜由惡水渡河，寇黎州，破碉子砦。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Jiading, the Miqang Xubuyou crossed the river at Eshui and raided Lizhou, breaking Diaozi Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In December 1208, Xubuyou crossed the E River and took Diaozi Stockade.

sentences.zh: 初，蓄卜弟悶巴至三沖為人所殺，又徙白水村渡於安靜砦，羌人患之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xubuyou's younger brother Menba had been killed at Sanchong; also the White Water village ferry had been moved to Anjing Stockade, which the Qiang resented.
translations.idiomatic: Menba had been killed at Sanchong and a ferry move angered the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 蓄卜遂與青羌詣邛部川，欲假道女兒城以入寇。

translations.literal: Xubuyou therefore joined the Qingyi and went to Qiongbu River, wishing to borrow the route through Nü'er city to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Xubuyou allied with Qingyi and sought passage through Nü'er city.

sentences.zh: 守臣楊子謨諜知之，數以貲遺其都王母，俾毋假道，時時饋米以濟其饑，蠻人德之。

translations.literal: Prefect Yang Zimo learned by espionage and repeatedly gave goods to their Queen Mother so she would not grant passage, sometimes sending grain to relieve their hunger; the Man were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yang Zimo bribed the Queen Mother with grain and gifts to deny passage.

sentences.zh: 會趙公庀代為郡，靳不與，蓄卜遂得假道渡河，攻茆坪砦，掠三松、蠶砂、橫山、三增、白羊諸村。

translations.literal: When Zhao Gongpi replaced him as prefect and was stingy, Xubuyou obtained passage, crossed the river, attacked Maoping Stockade, and plundered Sansong, Cansha, Hengshan, Sanzeng, Baiyang, and other villages.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Gongpi refused aid, Xubuyou crossed and raided many villages.

sentences.zh: 郡遣西兵將党壽禦之，失利，復遣統領王光世往。

translations.literal: The prefecture sent western troops under Dang Shou to resist; they were defeated, and Commander Wang Guangshi was sent.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Shou failed; Wang Guangshi was sent.

sentences.zh: 羌人由茆坪以革船渡河，光世憚之，留屯三沖不敢進。

translations.literal: The Qiang crossed at Maoping in leather boats; Guangshi feared them, halted at Sanchong, and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi feared their leather boats and halted at Sanchong.

sentences.zh: 羌人焚掠既盡，渡河而歸。

translations.literal: After the Qiang had burned and plundered everything, they crossed the river and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang looted and withdrew across the river.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，復寇黎州良溪砦，官軍敗績。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, they again raided Liangxi Stockade at Lizhou; government troops were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In February they raided Liangxi Stockade and defeated government troops.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，蓄卜降。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year, Xubuyou surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In February 1215, Xubuyou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 蓄卜連年入寇，皆青羌曳失索助之，守臣袁郐冉遣安靜砦總轄杜軫招降之。

translations.literal: Xubuyou had raided for years with Qingyi help; prefect Yuan Tai sent Du Zhen of Anjing Stockade to win them over.
translations.idiomatic: Xubuyou had raided with Qingyi aid until Du Zhen pacified him.

sentences.zh: 他如浮浪蠻、白蠻、烏蒙蠻、阿宗蠻，則其地各有所服屬云。

translations.literal: As for the Jinglang, Bai, Wumeng, and Azong Man, each territory had its own subordination.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglang, Bai, Wumeng, and Azong each had their own lords.

sentences.zh: 敘州三路蠻：西北曰董蠻，正西曰石門部，東南曰南廣蠻。

translations.literal: The three-route Man of Xuzhou: to the northwest are the Dong Man, directly west the Shimen division, and to the southeast the Nanguang Man.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou's three routes were Dong Man northwest, Shimen west, and Nanguang southeast.

sentences.zh: 董蠻在馬湖江右，韈侯國也。

translations.literal: The Dong Man are on the right bank of the Mahu River—the Wuhou state.
translations.idiomatic: The Dong Man lived on the Mahu River—the Wuhou state.

sentences.zh: 唐羈縻馴、騁、浪、商四州之地。

translations.literal: The territory of the four Tang jimi prefectures Xun, Cheng, Lang, and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: They held the four Tang jimi prefectures Xun, Cheng, Lang, and Shang.

sentences.zh: 其酋董氏，宋初有董舂惜者貢馬，自稱「馬湖路三十七部落都王子」。

translations.literal: Their chieftains were of the Dong clan; in early Song there was Dong Chunxi who offered horses, styling himself "Prince of the Thirty-Seven Tribes of the Mahu Road."
translations.idiomatic: Chieftain Dong Chunxi offered horses as prince of thirty-seven Mahu tribes.

sentences.zh: 其地北近犍為之沭川賴因砦。

translations.literal: Their territory bordered the Laiyin Stockade of Moshui in Qianwei to the north.
translations.idiomatic: They bordered Qianwei's Laiyin Stockade to the north.

sentences.zh: 砦厄蠻險，蠻數寇抄。

translations.literal: The stockade blocked Man defiles; the Man frequently raided.
translations.idiomatic: The stockade guarded a pass the Man often raided.

sentences.zh: 熙寧、紹聖中，朝廷皆為徙賴因監押駐榮丁砦，而以縣吏控截。

translations.literal: In the Xining and Shaosheng eras the court moved the Laiyin post commander to Rongding Stockade and used county clerks to control them.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining and Shaosheng the post was moved to Rongding and county clerks controlled the tribes.

sentences.zh: 政和五年，始改差監押充知砦事，蠻寇掠如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenghe, post commanders were first made stockade magistrates; Man raiding continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 1115, post commanders became magistrates but raiding continued.

sentences.zh: 南廣蠻在敘州慶符縣以西，為州十有四。

translations.literal: The Nanguang Man were west of Qingfu County in Xuzhou, with fourteen prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Nanguang Man west of Qingfu had fourteen prefectures.

sentences.zh: 大觀三年，有夷酋羅永順、楊光榮、李世恭等各以地內屬，詔建滋、純、祥三州，後皆廢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daguan, chieftains Luo Yongshun, Yang Guangrong, and Li Shigong each submitted lands; edicts established Zi, Chun, and Xiang prefectures—all later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1109, three chiefs submitted land; three prefectures were created then abolished.

sentences.zh: 石門蕃部與臨洮土羌接，唐曲、播等十二州之地。

translations.literal: The Shimen Fan tribes bordered the Lintao native Qiang; they held the twelve Tang prefectures Qu, Bo, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Shimen tribes bordered Lintao Qiang in twelve Tang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 俗椎髻、披氈、佩刀，居必欄棚，不喜耕稼，多畜牧。

translations.literal: Their custom was topknots, felt cloaks, and swords; they lived in palisaded lodges, disliked farming, and mostly herded.
translations.idiomatic: They wore topknots and felt, lived in palisades, and herded rather than farmed.

sentences.zh: 其人精悍善戰鬥，自馬湖、南廣諸族皆畏之。

translations.literal: Their people were fierce and skilled in battle; the Mahu and Nanguang tribes all feared them.
translations.idiomatic: They were fierce fighters feared by Mahu and Nanguang tribes.

sentences.zh: 蓋古浪稽、魯望諸部也。

translations.literal: They were the ancient Langji and Luwang tribes.
translations.idiomatic: They were the ancient Langji and Luwang tribes.

sentences.zh: 威州保霸蠻者，唐保、霸二州也。

translations.literal: The Wei and Ba Man of Weizhou were the Tang prefectures Bao and Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou's Wei-Ba Man were Tang Bao and Ba prefectures.

sentences.zh: 天寶中所置，後陷沒。

translations.literal: Established in the Tianbao era, they later fell.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Tianbao, they later fell to rebels.

sentences.zh: 酋董氏，世有其地，與威州相錯，因羈縻焉。

translations.literal: Chieftains of the Dong clan held the land for generations, interlocking with Weizhou, and were therefore jimi.
translations.idiomatic: The Dong clan held the land jimi alongside Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 保州有董仲元、霸州有董永錫者，嘉祐及熙寧中皆嘗請命於朝。

translations.literal: Dong Zhongyuan of Bao and Dong Yongxi of Ba both requested appointments in the Jiayou and Xining eras.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongyuan of Bao and Dong Yongxi of Ba sought offices in Jiayou and Xining.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，知成都龐恭孫始建言開拓，置官吏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, Chengdu prefect Pang Gongsun first proposed opening and settling the region with officials.
translations.idiomatic: In 1113, Pang Gongsun proposed establishing officials there.

sentences.zh: 於是以董舜咨保州地為祺州，董彥博霸州地為亨州，授舜咨刺史，彥博團練使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Dong Shunzi's Bao lands became Qi Prefecture and Dong Yanbo's Ba lands became Heng Prefecture; Shunzi was made prefect and Yanbo regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Bao became Qi and Ba became Heng; Shunzi and Yanbo were appointed.

sentences.zh: 舜咨尋遷觀察使；

translations.literal: Shunzi was soon promoted to observation commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Shunzi became observation commissioner;

sentences.zh: 彥博留後，遂為節度使。

translations.literal: Yanbo became military commissioner and then frontier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo became military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 詔成都給居第、田十二頃。

translations.literal: An edict granted them residences and twelve qing of fields at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu granted them houses and twelve qing of land.

sentences.zh: 二州經費歲用錢一萬二千一百緡，米麥一萬四千七百石，絹二千八百五十匹，糸由布、綾綿、茶、鹽、銀等不預焉。

translations.literal: The two prefectures' annual expenses were twelve thousand one hundred strings of cash, fourteen thousand seven hundred shi of grain, two thousand eight hundred fifty bolts of silk—not counting cloth, brocade, tea, salt, and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Annual costs were twelve thousand strings, fourteen thousand seven hundred shi of grain, and two thousand eight hundred fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 後皆為砦。

translations.literal: Later both became stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Later both became stockades.

sentences.zh: 茂州諸部落，蓋、塗、靜、當、直、時、飛、宕、恭等九州蠻也。

translations.literal: The tribes of Maozhou were the Man of the nine prefectures Gai, Tu, Jing, Dang, Zhi, Shi, Fei, Dang, and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhou tribes were nine prefectural Man groups.

sentences.zh: 蠻自推一人為州將，治其眾，而常詣茂州受約束。

translations.literal: The Man each chose a prefectural general to govern their masses and regularly came to Maozhou to receive constraints.
translations.idiomatic: Each tribe chose a general and submitted to Maozhou.

sentences.zh: 茂州居群蠻之中，地不過數十里，宋初無城隍，惟植鹿角自固。

translations.literal: Maozhou lay amid the tribes, its territory only several tens of li; in early Song there were no walls, only antler palisades for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhou had no walls in early Song, only antler fences.

sentences.zh: 蠻乘夜屢入寇，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: The Man repeatedly raided by night and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Night raids caused great suffering.

sentences.zh: 熙寧八年，相率詣州請築城，知州事范百常實主是役。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xining they collectively came to the prefecture requesting a walled city; Prefect Fan Baichang truly directed the work.
translations.idiomatic: In 1075, tribes asked for walls; Fan Baichang built them.

sentences.zh: 蠻以為侵其地，率眾奄至，百常擊走之，乃合靜、時等蠻來寇。

translations.literal: The Man thought their land was encroached upon, gathered suddenly, and Baichang drove them off; then the Jing, Shi, and other tribes joined to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes thought land was seized and attacked; others joined the raid.

sentences.zh: 百常拒守凡七十日。

translations.literal: Baichang held out for seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: Baichang held out seventy days.

sentences.zh: 詔遣王中正將陝西兵來援，入恭州、宕州，誅殺頗眾，蠻乃降。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Wang Zhongzheng leading Shaanxi troops to aid; entering Gong and Dang prefectures he killed many and the Man submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongzheng relieved the siege, killed many in Gong and Dang, and the Man submitted.

sentences.zh: 政和五年，有直州將郅永壽、湯延俊、董承有等各以地內屬，詔以永壽地建壽寧軍，延俊、承有地置延寧軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenghe, the Zhi prefectural generals Zhi Yongshou, Tang Yanjun, and Dong Chengyou each submitted lands; an edict made Yongshou's territory Shouning Army and Yanjun and Chengyou's territory Yanning Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1115, three generals submitted land; Shouning and Yanning armies were created.

sentences.zh: 時威州亦建亨、祺二州，然亨至威才九十里，壽寧距茂才五里，在大早江之外，非扼控之所，未幾皆廢。

translations.literal: At the time Weizhou also established Heng and Qi prefectures, but Heng was only ninety li from Wei and Shouning only five li from Mao, beyond the Dazao River—not places to control passes—and soon all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Heng and Qi were too close and poorly placed; soon all were abolished.

sentences.zh: 七年，塗、靜、時、飛等州蠻復反茂州，殺掠千餘人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Tu, Jing, Shi, and Fei tribes rebelled again at Maozhou, killing and plundering more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In 1117, Tu, Jing, Shi, and Fei tribes rebelled at Maozhou, killing over a thousand.

sentences.zh: 知成都周燾遣兵馬鈐轄張永鐸等擊之，畏懦不敢進，皆坐黜。

translations.literal: Chengdu prefect Zhou Tao sent military commander Zhang Yongduo and others to attack; they were cowardly and dared not advance—all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongduo was sent but dared not advance and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 以孫羲叟節制綿、茂軍，於是中軍將種友直等破其都祿板舍原諸族，蠻敗散。

translations.literal: Sun Yisou was made commander of Mian and Mao armies; then Central Army General Zhong Youzhi and others broke the Dulubansheyuan tribes and the Man scattered in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yisou took command; Zhong Youzhi routed the Dulubansheyuan tribes.

sentences.zh: 其酋旺烈等詣茂州請降，乃班師。

translations.literal: Their chieftain Wanglie and others came to Maozhou to surrender, and the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftain Wanglie surrendered and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 授旺烈官，月給茶彩。

translations.literal: Wanglie was granted office and given tea and silks monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Wanglie received office and monthly tea and silks.

sentences.zh: 自後蠻亦驕。

translations.literal: Afterward the Man also grew arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes grew arrogant again.

sentences.zh: 宣和五年，宕、恭、直諸部落入寇。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuanhe, the Dang, Gong, and Zhi tribes raided.
translations.idiomatic: In 1123, Dang, Gong, and Zhi tribes raided.

sentences.zh: 六年，塗、靜蠻復犯茂州云。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Tu and Jing Man again attacked Maozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1124, Tu and Jing attacked Maozhou again.

sentences.zh: 渝州蠻者，古板蚒七姓蠻，唐南平獠也。

translations.literal: The Yuzhou Man were the ancient Banpan seven-surname Man, the Tang Nanping Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou Man were the ancient seven-surname Banpan Man, Tang Nanping Liao.

sentences.zh: 其地西南接烏蠻、昆明、哥蠻、大小播州，部族數十居之。

translations.literal: Their territory southwest bordered Wuman, Kunming, Ge Man, and greater and lesser Bozhou; dozens of tribal groups dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: They bordered Wuman, Kunming, and Bozhou; dozens of tribes lived there.

sentences.zh: 治平中，熟夷李光吉、梁秀等三族據其地，各有眾數千家。

translations.literal: In the Zhiping era the acculturated Yi Li Guangji, Liang Xiu, and three clans held the land, each with thousands of households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiping, Li Guangji and Liang Xiu held the land with thousands of households each.

sentences.zh: 間以威勢脅誘漢戶，有不從者屠之，沒入土田。

translations.literal: From time to time they used force to coerce Han households; those who refused were slaughtered and their fields seized.
translations.idiomatic: They coerced Han settlers, killing resisters and seizing fields.

sentences.zh: 往往投充客戶，謂之納身，稅賦皆裏胥代償。

translations.literal: Many became attached clients called "body-submission"; taxes were all paid by village clerks on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Many became dependent clients; village clerks paid their taxes.

sentences.zh: 藏匿亡命，數以其徒偽為生獠動邊民，官軍追捕，輒遁去，習以為常，密賂黠民覘守令動靜，稍築城堡，繕器甲。

translations.literal: They harbored fugitives, often sent followers disguised as raw Liao to stir border people; when government troops pursued they always escaped—this became habitual; they secretly bribed clever locals to watch officials, gradually built forts, and prepared arms.
translations.idiomatic: They harbored fugitives, spied on officials, and built forts and arms.

sentences.zh: 遠近患之。

translations.literal: Near and far were troubled by them.
translations.idiomatic: The region suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，轉運使孫固、判官張詵使兵馬使馮儀、弁簡、杜安行圖之，以禍福開諭，因進兵，復賓化砦，平蕩三族。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, Transport Commissioner Sun Gu and Adjutant Zhang Shen sent military officers Feng Yi, Bian Jian, and Du Anxing to plan against them, opening persuasion with fortune and disaster, then advancing troops, recovering Binhua Stockade, and pacifying the three clans.
translations.idiomatic: In 1070, Sun Gu and Zhang Shen recovered Binhua and pacified three clans.

sentences.zh: 以其地賦民，凡得租三萬五千石，絲綿一萬六千兩。

translations.literal: Their land was assigned to the people; in all there were thirty-five thousand shi of rent and sixteen thousand liang of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The land yielded thirty-five thousand shi rent and sixteen thousand liang silk.

sentences.zh: 以賓化砦為隆化縣，隸涪州；

translations.literal: Binhua Stockade was made Longhua County, subordinate to Fu Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Binhua became Longhua County under Fu Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 建榮懿、扶歡兩砦。

translations.literal: Rongyi and Fuhuan stockades were established.
translations.idiomatic: Rongyi and Fuhuan stockades were built.

sentences.zh: 其外銅佛壩者，隸渝州南川縣，地皆膏腴。

translations.literal: Beyond that, Tongfo Dam was subordinate to Nanchuan County in Yuzhou; the land was all fertile.
translations.idiomatic: Tongfo Dam in Nanchuan was fertile.

sentences.zh: 自光吉等平，他部族據有之。

translations.literal: After Guangji and the others were pacified, other tribal groups held it.
translations.idiomatic: Other tribes occupied the land after Guangji's defeat.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因補其土人王才進充巡檢，委之控扼。

translations.literal: The court therefore appointed the native Wang Caijin as inspector and entrusted him with control.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Caijin was made inspector to control the region.

sentences.zh: 才進死，部族無所統，數出盜邊。

translations.literal: When Caijin died the tribes had no leader and repeatedly raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: After Caijin died, tribes raided without a leader.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命熊本討平之，建為南平軍，以渝州南川、涪州隆化隸焉。

translations.literal: The court ordered Xiong Ben to pacify them and established Nanping Army, with Nanchuan of Yuzhou and Longhua of Fu subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Ben pacified them and created Nanping Army.

sentences.zh: 元豐四年，有楊光震者，助官軍破乞弟，殺其党阿訛。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanfeng, Yang Guangzhen aided government troops in defeating Qidi and killed his partisan A'e.
translations.idiomatic: In 1081, Yang Guangzhen helped defeat Qidi and killed A'e.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，木攀首領趙泰、播州夷族楊光榮各以地內屬，詔建溱、播二州，後皆廢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan, the Mupan chieftain Zhao Tai and the Bozhou Yi Yang Guangrong each submitted lands; edicts established Qin and Bo prefectures—later all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1108, Zhao Tai and Yang Guangrong submitted land; Qin and Bo were created then abolished.

sentences.zh: 黔州、涪州徼外有西南夷部，漢訸訫郡，唐南寧州、訸訫、昆明、東謝、南謝、西趙、充州諸蠻也。

translations.literal: Beyond the borders of Qian and Fu were southwestern Yi tribes—the Han Zangge commandery; Tang Nanning, Zangge, Kunming, Eastern Xie, Southern Xie, Western Zhao, and Chong prefecture Man.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Qian and Fu were southwestern tribes of Han Zangge and Tang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 其地東北直黔、涪，西北接嘉、敘，東連荊楚，南出宜、桂。

translations.literal: Their territory ran northeast straight to Qian and Fu, northwest connecting Jia and Xu, east linking Jing-Chu, south reaching Yi and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands stretched from Qian-Fu to Jia-Xu, Jing-Chu, and Yi-Gui.

sentences.zh: 俗椎髻、左衽，或編發；

translations.literal: Their custom was topknots and left-lapelled dress, or braided hair;
translations.idiomatic: They wore topknots, left-lapelled dress, or braids;

sentences.zh: 隨畜牧遷徙亡常，喜險阻，善戰鬥。

translations.literal: they followed herds in migration without fixed abode, loved defiles, and were skilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: they migrated with herds, loved mountains, and fought well.

sentences.zh: 部族共一姓，雖各有君長，而風俗略同。

translations.literal: The tribes shared one surname; though each had its own chief, customs were much the same.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes shared a surname and similar customs despite separate chiefs.

sentences.zh: 宋初以來，有龍蕃、方蕃、張蕃、石蕃、羅蕃者，號「五姓蕃」，皆常奉職貢，受爵命。

translations.literal: Since early Song there were Long, Fang, Zhang, Shi, and Luo tribes, called the "Five-Surname Fan," all regularly performing duties and tribute and receiving ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Since early Song the Five-Surname Fan of Long, Fang, Zhang, Shi, and Luo tribute regularly.

sentences.zh: 治平四年十二月，知靜蠻軍、蕃落使、守天聖大王龍異閣等入見，詔以異閣為武甯將軍，其屬二百四十一人各授將軍及郎將。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Zhiping, the Quiet-the-Man Army commissioner and tribal commissioner, Guardian of Heavenly Sagacity King Long Yige, and others came to audience; Yige was made General of Martial Pacification and two hundred forty-one followers were given general and commandant ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In 1067, Long Yige and two hundred forty-one followers received ranks.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，張蕃乞添貢奉人至三百，詔故事以七十人為額，不許。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng, the Zhang Fan requested increasing tribute personnel to three hundred; an edict said precedent fixed seventy and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1082, Zhang Fan's request for three hundred tribute envoys was denied; seventy was the quota.

sentences.zh: 七年，西南程蕃乞貢方物，願依五姓蕃例注籍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the southwestern Cheng Fan requested to offer local products and wished to register by the Five-Surname Fan precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1084, Cheng Fan asked to register like the Five-Surname Fan.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 元祐二年，西南石蕃石以定等齎表，自稱「西平州武聖軍」。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanyou, the southwestern Shi Fan Shi Yiding and others brought a memorial, styling themselves "Martial Sage Army of Xiping Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: In 1087, Shi Yiding styled his group the Martial Sage Army of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 禮部言元豐著令以五年一貢為限，今年限未及。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said Yuanfeng regulations fixed tribute once every five years and this year the term had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites noted the five-year tribute interval had not elapsed.

sentences.zh: 詔特令入貢。

translations.literal: An edict specially allowed them to enter tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The court allowed special tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年，八年，紹聖四年，龍蕃皆貢方物。

translations.literal: In the fifth and eighth years and the fourth year of Shaosheng, the Long Fan all offered local products.
translations.idiomatic: Long Fan tribute came in 1090, 1093, and 1097.

sentences.zh: 龍氏于諸姓為最大，其貢奉尤頻數，使者便衣布袍，至假伶人之衣入見，蓋實貧陋，所冀者恩賞而已。

translations.literal: Among all surnames the Long were largest; their tribute was especially frequent; envoys wore plain cloth robes and even borrowed actors' clothes to enter audience—they were truly poor and shabby and desired only imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: The Long were largest and poorest, borrowing clothes for audience and seeking only favor.

sentences.zh: 故事，蠻夷入貢，雖交詾、於闐之屬皆御前殿見之，獨此諸蕃見於後殿，蓋卑之也。

translations.literal: By precedent, when Man and Yi entered tribute, even Jiaozhi and Khotan were received in the main hall; only these Fan were received in the rear hall—clearly to demean them.
translations.idiomatic: Other tributaries met in the main hall; these Fan met in the rear hall as a slight.

sentences.zh: 元符二年，又有牟韋蕃入貢，詔以進奉人韋公憂、公市、公利等為郎將。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfu, the Mouwei Fan also came; an edict made tribute bearers Wei Gongyou, Gongshi, and Gongli commandants.
translations.idiomatic: In 1099, Mouwei Fan envoys became commandants.

sentences.zh: 諸蕃部族數十，獨五姓最著，程氏、韋氏皆比附五姓，故號「西南七蕃」云。

translations.literal: Among dozens of Fan tribes only the Five Surnames were most prominent; the Cheng and Wei clans all attached to the Five Surnames, and so they were called the "Southwestern Seven Fan."
translations.idiomatic: With Cheng and Wei attached, they were called the Southwestern Seven Fan.

sentences.zh: 施州蠻者，夔路徼外熟夷，南接訸訫諸蠻，又與順、富、高、溪四州蠻相錯，蓋唐彭水蠻也。

translations.literal: The Shi Prefecture Man were acculturated Yi beyond the Kuizhou circuit, south connecting to Zangge Man and interlocking with the Shun, Fu, Gao, and Xi four prefecture tribes—Tang Pengshui Man.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Prefecture Man were Kuizhou acculturated Yi linked to Zangge and four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，施蠻嘗入寇，詔以鹽與之，且許其以粟轉易，蠻大悅，自是不為邊患。

translations.literal: In Xianping the Shi Man once raided; an edict gave them salt and allowed barter with grain; the Man were greatly pleased and from then on were no border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Salt and grain trade pacified Shi Man raids in Xianping.

sentences.zh: 後因饑，又以金銀倍實直質于官易粟，官不能禁。

translations.literal: Later because of famine they again pawned gold and silver at double true value to the government for grain; officials could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: In famine they pawned gold and silver to officials for grain.

sentences.zh: 熙甯六年，詔施州蠻以金銀質米者，估實直；

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xining, an edict ordered that when Shi Prefecture Man pawned grain with gold and silver, true value should be estimated;
translations.idiomatic: In 1073, pawned gold and silver for grain had to be fairly valued;

sentences.zh: 如七年不贖，則變易之。

translations.literal: if not redeemed in seven years it should be sold off.
translations.idiomatic: unredeemed pawns were sold after seven years.

sentences.zh: 著為令。

translations.literal: This was enacted as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The rule was codified.

sentences.zh: 熊本經制淯井事，蠻酋田現等內附，夔路轉運判官董鉞、副使孫珪、知施州寇平，皆以招納功被賞。

translations.literal: When Xiong Ben directed Qijing affairs, the Man chieftain Tian Xian and others submitted; Kuizhou transport adjutant Dong E, vice commissioner Sun Gui, and Shi Prefecture prefect Kou Ping were all rewarded for winning them over.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Ben won over Tian Xian; Dong E, Sun Gui, and Kou Ping were rewarded.

sentences.zh: 施、黔比近蠻，子弟精悍，用木弩藥箭，戰鬥し捷，朝廷嘗團結為忠義勝軍。

translations.literal: Shi and Qian neighboring Man had stalwart youths who used wooden crossbows and poisoned arrows and were swift in battle; the court once organized them as the Loyal and Righteous Victory Army.
translations.idiomatic: Their youths used poisoned crossbows; the court formed the Loyal and Righteous Victory Army.

sentences.zh: 其後，瀘州、淯井、石泉蠻叛，皆獲其用。

translations.literal: Afterward, when Luzhou, Qijing, and Shiquan Man rebelled, they were all put to use.
translations.idiomatic: They helped suppress Luzhou, Qijing, and Shiquan rebellions.

sentences.zh: 高州蠻，故夜郎也，在涪州西南。

translations.literal: The Gao Prefecture Man were ancient Yelang, southwest of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Prefecture Man were ancient Yelang southwest of Fu.

sentences.zh: 宋初、其酋田景遷以地內附，賜名珍州，拜為刺史。

translations.literal: In early Song their chieftain Tian Jingqian submitted lands, was granted the name Zhen Prefecture, and appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jingqian submitted and received Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 景遷以郡多火災，請易今名。

translations.literal: Jingqian, because the commandery had many fires, requested the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Jingqian renamed the prefecture after frequent fires.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，有駱解下、上族納土，復以珍州名云。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan, the Luo upper and lower clans submitted land and the name Zhen Prefecture was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 1108, the Luo clans restored the name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 瀘州西南徼外，古羌夷之地，漢以來王侯國以百數，獨夜郎、滇、邛都、溋、昆明、徙、都、冉垆ζ、白馬氐為最大。

translations.literal: Beyond southwestern Luzhou were ancient Qiang-Yi lands; since Han there had been hundreds of kingdoms—only Yelang, Dian, Qiongdou, Wen, Kunming, Xi, Zuodu, Ranmang, and White Horse Di were greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of Luzhou lay ancient kingdoms; Yelang, Dian, Qiongdou, and others were greatest.

sentences.zh: 夜郎，在漢屬訸訫郡，今涪州之西，溱、播、珍等州封域是也；

translations.literal: Yelang in Han belonged to Zangge commandery—today west of Fu Prefecture, the territories of Qin, Bo, Zhen, and other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Yelang was Han Zangge—today west of Fu, Qin, Bo, and Zhen;

sentences.zh: 滇，在漢為益州郡，今姚州善闡之地是也；

translations.literal: Dian in Han was Yizhou commandery—today the Shanchan lands of Yao Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Dian was Han Yizhou—today Yao Prefecture Shanchan;

sentences.zh: 邛都，溋州會同川與吐蕃接，今邛部川蠻所居也；

translations.literal: Qiongdou, Huitong River of Wen Prefecture bordering Tibet—today where Qiongbu River Man dwell;
translations.idiomatic: Qiongdou was Wen's Huitong River—today's Qiongbu Man;

sentences.zh: 溋，今溋州；

translations.literal: Wen is today's Wen Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Wen is today's Wen Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 昆明，在黔、瀘徼外，今西南蕃部所居也；

translations.literal: Kunming, beyond Qian and Lu borders—today where southwestern Fan tribes dwell;
translations.idiomatic: Kunming lay beyond Qian and Lu—today's southwestern Fan;

sentences.zh: 徙，今雅州嚴道地；

translations.literal: Xi is today's Yazhou Yandao territory;
translations.idiomatic: Xi is Yazhou Yandao;

sentences.zh: 都，在黎州南，今兩林及野川蠻所居地是也；

translations.literal: Zuodu, south of Lizhou—today where Lianglin and Yechuan Man dwell;
translations.idiomatic: Zuodu was south of Lizhou—today's Lianglin and Yechuan;

sentences.zh: 冉垆ζ，今茂州蠻、汶山夷地是也；

translations.literal: Ranmang is today's Maozhou Man and Wenshan Yi territory;
translations.idiomatic: Ranmang is Maozhou and Wenshan;

sentences.zh: 白馬氐，在漢為武都郡，今階州、汶州，蓋羌類也：此皆巴蜀西南徼外蠻夷也。

translations.literal: White Horse Di in Han was Wudou commandery—today Jie and Wen prefectures, basically Qiang type: all these are southwestern Man and Yi beyond Ba-Shu.
translations.idiomatic: White Horse Di was Han Wudou—today Jie and Wen; all were Ba-Shu frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 自黔、恭以西，至涪、瀘、嘉、敘，自階又折而東，南至威、茂、黎、雅，被邊十餘郡，綿亙數千里，剛夷惡獠，殆千萬計。

translations.literal: From Qian and Gong west to Fu, Lu, Jia, and Xu, from Jie bending east to Wei, Mao, Li, and Ya—more than ten border commanderies spanning several thousand li, fierce Yi and wicked Liao, nearly ten million in all.
translations.idiomatic: Ten border prefectures held millions of fierce tribes.

sentences.zh: 自治平之末訖于靖康，大抵皆通互市，奉職貢，雖時有剽掠，如鼠竊狗偷，不能為深患。

translations.literal: From late Zhiping until Jingkang they mostly traded and sent tribute; though there were raids, like rats and dogs stealing, they could not become deep trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Until Jingkang they mostly traded; raids were petty.

sentences.zh: 參考古今，辨其封域，以見琛贐之自至，梯航之所及者爾。

translations.literal: Comparing ancient and modern and distinguishing their territories shows only that tribute came of itself and where ladders and ships could reach.
translations.idiomatic: This account maps where tribute and trade reached.

sentences.zh: 若夫邊荊楚、交廣，則系之溪峒云。

translations.literal: As for bordering Jing-Chu and Jiaoguang, that belongs under the stream gorges.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes bordering Jing-Chu and Guang are treated under stream gorges.

sentences.zh: 淯水夷者，羈縻十州五囤蠻也，雜種夷獠散居溪穀中。

translations.literal: The Yu River Yi were jimi ten-prefecture five-stockade Man, mixed Yi and Liao scattered in stream valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Yu River Yi were ten jimi prefectures and five stockades in the valleys.

sentences.zh: 慶曆初，瀘州言：「管下溪峒十州，有唐及本朝所賜州額，今烏蠻王子得蓋居其地。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingli, Luzhou reported: "Under jurisdiction are ten gorge prefectures with Tang and our dynasty grants of prefectural titles; now the Wuman prince Degai dwells in their lands.
translations.idiomatic: In 1041, Luzhou reported Wuman prince Degai held ten gorge prefectures.

sentences.zh: 部族最盛，旁有舊姚州，廢已久，得蓋願得州名以長夷落。

translations.literal: His tribe is strongest; beside it is old Yao Prefecture, long abolished; Degai wishes a prefectural name to extend his Yi following."
translations.idiomatic: Degai sought restoration of abolished Yao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 」詔復建姚州，以得蓋為刺史，鑄印賜之。

translations.literal: " An edict restored Yao Prefecture, made Degai prefect, and cast a seal for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was restored; Degai became prefect with a seal.

sentences.zh: 得蓋死，其子竊號「羅氏鬼主」。

translations.literal: When Degai died, his son usurped the title "Ghost Master of the Luo Clan."
translations.idiomatic: Degai's son took the title Ghost Master of the Luo Clan.

sentences.zh: 鬼主死，子僕射襲其號，浸弱不能令諸族。

translations.literal: When the Ghost Master died, his son Pushe inherited the title and gradually weakened, unable to command the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Pushe succeeded but could not command the tribes.

sentences.zh: 烏蠻有二酋領：曰晏子，曰斧望個恕，常入漢地鬻馬。

translations.literal: Among the Wuman were two chieftains: Yanzi and Fuwang Geshu, who often entered Han territory to sell horses.
translations.idiomatic: Two Wuman chiefs, Yanzi and Fuwang Geshu, traded horses in Han lands.

sentences.zh: 晏子所居，直長寧、寧遠以南，斧望個恕所居，直納溪、江安以東，皆僕夜諸部也。

translations.literal: Yanzi dwelt directly south of Changning and Ningyuan; Fuwang Geshu dwelt directly east of Naxi and Jiang'an—all Buye tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzi held Changning south; Geshu held Naxi east—all Buye tribes.

sentences.zh: 晏子距漢地絕近，猶有淯井之阻。

translations.literal: Yanzi was extremely close to Han territory, though Qijing still blocked the way.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzi was very close, though Qijing lay between.

sentences.zh: 斧望個恕近納溪，以舟下瀘不過半日。

translations.literal: Fuwang Geshu was near Naxi; by boat down to Lu took less than half a day.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu was near Naxi—a half day's sail to Lu.

sentences.zh: 二酋浸強大，擅劫晏州山外六姓及納溪二十四姓生夷。

translations.literal: The two chiefs grew ever stronger and monopolized raiding the six surnames beyond Yanzhou mountain and the twenty-four surnames of raw Yi at Naxi.
translations.idiomatic: Both grew strong and preyed on Yanzhou and Naxi tribes.

sentences.zh: 夷弱小，皆相與供其寶。

translations.literal: The weaker Yi all together supplied their treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Weaker Yi paid them tribute.

sentences.zh: 熙寧七年，六姓夷自淯井謀入寇，命熊本經制之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xining the six-surname Yi plotted invasion from Qijing; Xiong Ben was ordered to direct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1074, six tribes plotted invasion; Xiong Ben was sent.

sentences.zh: 景思忠戰沒，本將蜀兵，募土丁及夷界黔州弩手，以毒矢射賊，賊驚潰。

translations.literal: Jing Sizhong died in battle; Ben led Shu troops, recruited local militia and Qian crossbowmen from the Yi border, shot the bandits with poisoned arrows, and the bandits fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Sizhong fell; Ben used poisoned arrows and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 於是山前後、長寧等十郡八姓及武都夷皆內附。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ten prefectures and eight surnames before and behind the mountains, Changning, and the Wudu Yi all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ten prefectures, eight surnames, and Wudu Yi submitted.

sentences.zh: 提點刑獄范百祿作文以誓之曰：

translations.literal: Judicial intendant Fan Bailu wrote a text to swear by, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Fan Bailu wrote an oath text:

sentences.zh: 蠢茲夷醜，淯溪之滸。

translations.literal: Foolish are these Yi villains, the bank of Yu Stream.
translations.idiomatic: Foolish Yi villains on the Yu Stream's bank,

sentences.zh: 為虺為豺，憑負固圉。

translations.literal: Serpents and wolves, relying on solid defenses.
translations.idiomatic: serpents and wolves in stout defenses,

sentences.zh: 殺人於貨，頭顱草莽。

translations.literal: Killing men for goods, heads strewn in the wild.
translations.idiomatic: killing for loot, heads in the wild.

sentences.zh: 莫慘燔炙，莫悲奴虜。

translations.literal: None more cruel than roasting alive, none sadder than enslavement.
translations.idiomatic: None crueler than burning alive; none sadder than slavery.

sentences.zh: 狃刦熟慝，胡可悉數。

translations.literal: Accustomed to plunder, how can all be counted?
translations.idiomatic: Their plunder—who can count it all?

sentences.zh: 疆吏苟玩，噤不敢語。

translations.literal: Frontier officials played careless and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials played careless and stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 奮若之歲，曾是強禦。

translations.literal: In the year of their pride they were strong foes.
translations.idiomatic: In their proud years they were fierce foes.

sentences.zh: 躑躅嘯聚，三壕、羅募。

translations.literal: Stamping and howling they gathered at Sanhao and Luomu.
translations.idiomatic: They gathered at Sanhao and Luomu, stamping and howling.

sentences.zh: 僨我將佐，戕我士伍。

translations.literal: They ruined our generals and slew our soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: They ruined our generals and slew our soldiers.

sentences.zh: 西南繹騷，帝赫斯怒。

translations.literal: The southwest was in turmoil; the emperor blazed with anger.
translations.idiomatic: The southwest seethed; the emperor blazed with anger.

sentences.zh: 帝怒伊何？

translations.literal: Why was the emperor angry?
translations.idiomatic: Why was he angry?

sentences.zh: 神聖文武。

translations.literal: Sacred and martial.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred and martial.

sentences.zh: 民所安樂，惟曰慈撫。

translations.literal: What the people find peace in, he calls cherishing and soothing.
translations.idiomatic: He soothes what brings the people peace.

sentences.zh: 民所疾苦，惟曰砭去。

translations.literal: What the people find bitter, he calls piercing and removing.
translations.idiomatic: He removes what brings the people pain.

sentences.zh: 乃用其良，應變是許。

translations.literal: Therefore he used the capable and permitted them to meet change.
translations.idiomatic: He used able men to meet the crisis.

sentences.zh: 粥熊裔孫，爰馭貔虎。

translations.literal: A descendant of the Mi-Xiong clan came to drive tigers.
translations.idiomatic: A Mi-Xiong descendant came to drive the army like tigers.

sentences.zh: 殲其渠酋，判其黨與。

translations.literal: He destroyed their chieftains and judged their factions.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed chiefs and broke their factions.

sentences.zh: 既奪之心，復斷右股。

translations.literal: Having taken their hearts, he also cut the right thigh.
translations.idiomatic: He broke their will and crippled their strength.

sentences.zh: 攝提孟陬，徂征有敘。

translations.literal: In the first month of Sheti, the campaign marched in order.
translations.idiomatic: In Sheti's first month the campaign marched in order.

sentences.zh: 背孤擊虛，深入厥阻。

translations.literal: Striking where they were exposed, he penetrated deep into their barriers.
translations.idiomatic: He struck their weak points and pierced their barriers.

sentences.zh: 兵從天下，鐵首其舉。

translations.literal: Troops came from all under heaven; iron heads raised the assault.
translations.idiomatic: Armies gathered; iron heads led the assault.

sentences.zh: 紛紜騰遝，莫敢嬰牾。

translations.literal: Tumbling and rushing, none dared resist.
translations.idiomatic: None dared resist the rushing host.

sentences.zh: 火其巢穴，及其亘貯。

translations.literal: He burned their nests and their stored goods.
translations.idiomatic: He burned nests and stores.

sentences.zh: 暨其貲畜，墟其林ＶＥ。

translations.literal: And their livestock; he laid waste to their groves.
translations.idiomatic: He seized livestock and laid waste groves.

sentences.zh: 殺傷系縲，以百千數。

translations.literal: Wounded and bound, they numbered in the hundreds and thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds and thousands were wounded and bound.

sentences.zh: 涇灘望風，悉力比附。

translations.literal: At Jingtan they watched the wind and strove to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingtan they submitted to the wind.

sentences.zh: 丁為帝民，地曰王土。

translations.literal: Men became the emperor's people; land became royal soil.
translations.idiomatic: Men became imperial subjects; land became royal soil.

sentences.zh: 投其器械，籍入官府。

translations.literal: They surrendered weapons and were registered into government stores.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons were registered in government stores.

sentences.zh: 百死一贖，莫保銅鼓。

translations.literal: One in a hundred might ransom life; none could keep bronze drums.
translations.idiomatic: Few ransomed life; bronze drums were seized.

sentences.zh: 歃盟神天，視此狗鼠。

translations.literal: They swore oaths to heaven and earth, looking on these as dogs and rats.
translations.idiomatic: They swore to heaven, treating rebels as vermin.

sentences.zh: 敢忘誅絕，以幹罪罟。

translations.literal: Daring to forget extermination and court punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet daring to forget extermination and court punishment.

sentences.zh: 乃稱上恩，俾復故處。

translations.literal: Then they praised imperial grace and were allowed to return to their old places.
translations.idiomatic: Then they praised grace and returned home.

sentences.zh: 殘醜厥角，泣血訴語：「天子之德，雨撸覆護。

translations.literal: The maimed turned their horns; weeping blood they pleaded: "The Son of Heaven's virtue covers us like rain and dew.
translations.idiomatic: The broken wept blood: "The Son of Heaven's grace covers us like rain.

sentences.zh: 三五噍類，請比涇仵。」

translations.literal: All creatures of mouth and breath beg to be like Jingtan's oxen."
translations.idiomatic: All living things beg mercy like Jingtan's cattle."

sentences.zh: 大邦有令，其戒警汝：天既汝貸，汝勿予侮。

translations.literal: The great state has orders—take warning: heaven has spared you; do not insult us.
translations.idiomatic: The court warned: heaven spared you—do not insult us.

sentences.zh: 惟十九姓，往安汝堵。

translations.literal: Only the nineteen surnames—go and settle your walls.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen surnames—settle your walls.

sentences.zh: 吏治汝責，汝力汝布。

translations.literal: Officials govern your duties; your labor, your cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Officials govern you; you labor and weave.

sentences.zh: 吏時汝耕，汝稻汝黍。

translations.literal: When officials timely plow for you, you have rice and millet.
translations.idiomatic: Officials help your plowing; you grow rice and millet.

sentences.zh: 懲創於今，無忄太往古。

translations.literal: Punishment from today forward—do not slacken as in the past.
translations.idiomatic: Punish today—do not slacken as before.

sentences.zh: 小有堡障，大有城戍。

translations.literal: Small places have stockades; large places have garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Small stockades, large garrisons.

sentences.zh: 汝或不聽，汝擊汝捕。

translations.literal: If you do not listen, you will be struck and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Disobey and you will be struck and captured.

sentences.zh: 尚有刦將，突騎強旅。

translations.literal: There are still raiding generals and swift cavalry hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Raiding generals and swift cavalry remain.

sentences.zh: 傅此黔軍，毒矢勁弩。

translations.literal: With this Qian army, poisoned arrows and strong crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Qian troops carry poisoned arrows and strong crossbows.

sentences.zh: 天不汝容，暴汝居所。

translations.literal: Heaven will not contain you; it will ravage your dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven will ravage your dwellings.

sentences.zh: 不汝遺育，悔于何取！

translations.literal: It will leave you no offspring—what regret could you have!
translations.idiomatic: No offspring will remain—what regret then!

sentences.zh: 立石于武寧砦。

translations.literal: A stone was erected at Wuning Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: A stone was set up at Wuning Stockade.

sentences.zh: 熊本言二酋桀黠，不羈縻之則諸蠻未易服，遂遣人說誘招納。

translations.literal: Xiong Ben said the two chiefs were crafty and fierce; unless they were jimi the tribes would not easily submit, and so he sent men to persuade and win them.
translations.idiomatic: Ben said Yanzi and Geshu must be jimi or tribes would not submit.

sentences.zh: 於是晏子、斧望個恕及僕夜皆願入貢，受王命。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yanzi, Fuwang Geshu, and Buye all wished to offer tribute and receive royal commands.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzi, Geshu, and Buye offered tribute and accepted commands.

sentences.zh: 晏子未及命而死，乃以個恕知歸來州，僕夜知姚州，以個恕之子乞弟、晏子之子沙取祿路並為把截將、西南夷部巡檢。

translations.literal: Yanzi died before appointment; Geshu was made prefect of Guilai, Buye prefect of Yao, and Geshu's son Qidi and Yanzi's son Shaqululu both made intercept generals and southwestern Yi inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzi died; Geshu got Guilai, Buye Yao; Qidi and Shaqululu became inspectors.

sentences.zh: 八年，俞州獠寇南州，獠酋阿訛率其黨奔個恕。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Yu Prefecture Liao raided Nan Prefecture; the Liao chieftain A'e led his faction to flee to Geshu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1075, A'e fled to Geshu after raiding Nan.

sentences.zh: 熊本重賞檄斬訛。

translations.literal: Xiong Ben offered heavy rewards in a dispatch to behead A'e.
translations.idiomatic: Ben offered a reward for A'e's head.

sentences.zh: 訛桀黠，習知邊境虛實，個恕匿不殺，詭降於納溪。

translations.literal: A'e was crafty and knew border realities; Geshu hid him and did not kill him, falsely surrendering at Naxi.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty A'e was hidden by Geshu, who feigned surrender at Naxi.

sentences.zh: 訛得不死，甚德個恕，為伺邊隙。

translations.literal: A'e thus escaped death and deeply thanked Geshu, spying for border openings.
translations.idiomatic: A'e survived and spied for Geshu.

sentences.zh: 會個恕老厭兵，以事屬乞弟，遂與訛侵諸部。

translations.literal: When Geshu grew old and weary of war he gave affairs to Qidi, who joined A'e in encroaching on the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Old Geshu handed power to Qidi, who joined A'e raiding tribes.

sentences.zh: 十年，羅苟夷犯納溪砦。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Luogou Yi attacked Naxi Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In 1077, Luogou Yi attacked Naxi Stockade.

sentences.zh: 初，砦民與羅苟夷競魚笱，誤毆殺之，吏為按驗。

translations.literal: Earlier, stockade people and Luogou Yi competed over fish weirs and mistakenly beat one to death; officials investigated.
translations.idiomatic: A fish-weir quarrel led to a killing investigated by officials.

sentences.zh: 夷已忿，謂：「漢殺吾人，官不嘗我骨價，反暴露之。

translations.literal: The Yi were already angry, saying: "Han killed our man; officials did not pay bone-price for us but exposed the body."
translations.idiomatic: The Yi raged that Han killed their man without paying blood-price.

sentences.zh: 」遂叛。

translations.literal: " They therefore rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: They rebelled.

sentences.zh: 提點刑獄穆曁向言：「納溪去瀘一舍，羅苟去納溪數里，今托事起端，若不加誅，則烏蠻觀望，為害不細。

translations.literal: Judicial intendant Mu Xian said: "Naxi is one stage from Lu; Luogou is several li from Naxi—if this beginning is not punished, Wuman will watch and the harm will not be slight."
translations.idiomatic: Mu Xian warned that failure to punish would encourage Wuman.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔涇原副總管韓存寶擊之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jingyuan vice overall commander Han Cunbao to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Han Cunbao was ordered to attack.

sentences.zh: 存寶召乞弟等犄角，討蕩五十六村，十三囤蠻乞降，願納土承賦租。

translations.literal: Cunbao summoned Qidi and others in pincer fashion, swept fifty-six villages, and thirteen stockade tribes begged surrender, wishing to submit land and pay rent.
translations.idiomatic: Cunbao swept fifty-six villages; thirteen tribes surrendered land and rent.

sentences.zh: 乃詔罷兵。

translations.literal: An edict then halted the army.
translations.idiomatic: The army was halted.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，乞弟率晏州夷合步騎六千至江安城下，責平羅苟之賞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng, Qidi led Yanzhou Yi with six thousand foot and horse to Jiang'an city, demanding reward for pacifying Luogou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1078, Qidi besieged Jiang'an demanding Luogou rewards.

sentences.zh: 城中守兵才數百，震恐不能授甲，蠻數日乃引去。

translations.literal: Defenders numbered only several hundred; terrified, they could not arm themselves; the Man withdrew after several days.
translations.idiomatic: Only hundreds defended; the Man withdrew after days.

sentences.zh: 知瀘州喬敘要欲與盟，遣梓夔都監王宣以兵二千守江安，仍奏以乞弟襲歸來州刺史。

translations.literal: Prefect Qiao Xuyao wished to make alliance and sent Zi-Kui overall inspector Wang Xuan with two thousand troops to hold Jiang'an, memorializing that Qidi succeed as Guilai prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Xuyao allied and asked Qidi succeed as Guilai prefect.

sentences.zh: 韓運遣小校楊舜之召乞弟拜敕，乞弟不出；

translations.literal: Han Yun sent junior officer Yang Shunzhi to summon Qidi to receive the edict; Qidi did not come out;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shunzhi summoned Qidi for the edict; he refused;

sentences.zh: 遣就賜之，亦不見；

translations.literal: sent to grant it at his place, and still he would not appear;
translations.idiomatic: sent to his camp, he still refused;

sentences.zh: 而令小蠻從舜之取敕以去。

translations.literal: but had a small Man take the edict from Shunzhi and leave.
translations.idiomatic: a small Man took the edict and left.

sentences.zh: 喬敘因沙取祿路以賄招乞弟，乃肯來。

translations.literal: Qiao Xuyao used Shaqululu's bribes to win Qidi, and only then did he come.
translations.idiomatic: Bribes through Shaqululu brought Qidi in.

sentences.zh: 三年，盟於納溪。

translations.literal: In the third year they allied at Naxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1080 they allied at Naxi.

sentences.zh: 蠻以為畏己，益悖慢。

translations.literal: The Man thought themselves feared and grew ever more insolent.
translations.idiomatic: The Man grew insolent, thinking themselves feared.

sentences.zh: 盟五日，遂以眾圍羅個牟族。

translations.literal: Five days after the alliance they surrounded the Luogemou clan with a host.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later they besieged Luogemou.

sentences.zh: 羅個牟，熊本所團結熟夷也。

translations.literal: Luogemou was acculturated Yi whom Xiong Ben had organized.
translations.idiomatic: Luogemou was Yi organized by Xiong Ben.

sentences.zh: 王宣往救之，蠻解圍，合力拒官軍。

translations.literal: Wang Xuan went to rescue them; the Man lifted the siege and combined to resist government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuan rescued them; the Man turned on government troops.

sentences.zh: 宣與一軍皆沒，事遂張，ㄞ召存寶授方略，統三將兵萬八千趨東川。

translations.literal: Xuan and his whole army perished; the affair grew large; the court summoned Cunbao for strategy; he commanded three generals with eighteen thousand troops hurrying to Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's army was destroyed; Cunbao was summoned with eighteen thousand men.

sentences.zh: 存寶怯懦不敢進，乞弟送款紿降，存寶信之，遂休兵於綿、梓、遂、資間。

translations.literal: Cunbao was cowardly and dared not advance; Qidi sent false surrender; Cunbao believed it and rested troops among Mian, Zi, Sui, and Zi.
translations.idiomatic: Cowardly Cunbao believed Qidi's false surrender and halted.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔以環慶副總管林廣代存寶，按寶逗撓，誅之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict made Huanqing vice overall commander Lin Guang replace Cunbao; Cunbao was investigated for delay and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Guang replaced and executed delaying Cunbao.

sentences.zh: 熟夷楊光震殺阿訛，詔林廣與光震同力討賊。

translations.literal: Acculturated Yi Yang Guangzhen killed A'e; an edict ordered Lin Guang and Guangzhen to join forces against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangzhen killed A'e; Lin Guang was ordered to join him.

sentences.zh: 乞弟恐，復送款。

translations.literal: Qidi was afraid and again sent surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qidi again offered surrender.

sentences.zh: 帝以其前後反覆，無真降意，督廣進師。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of his repeated reversals, had no true intent to submit, and urged Guang to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doubted Qidi and urged Guang forward.

sentences.zh: 廣遂破樂共城，至鬥蒲村，斬首二千五百級。

translations.literal: Guang then broke Le Gong city, reaching Doupu village, beheading two thousand five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Guang took Le Gong and beheaded twenty-five hundred at Doupu.

sentences.zh: 次落婆，乞弟乃納降。

translations.literal: Next at Luopo, Qidi finally submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At Luopo Qidi submitted.

sentences.zh: 廣盛陳兵以受之，對語良久，乞弟疑有變，引眾遁。

translations.literal: Guang arrayed troops to receive him; after long talk Qidi suspected change and fled with his host.
translations.idiomatic: Guang received him; Qidi suspected treachery and fled.

sentences.zh: 廣帥兵深入，會大雨雪，浹旬始次老人山，山形劍立。

translations.literal: Guang led troops deep in; meeting great rain and snow, after ten days he reached Old Man Mountain, its peaks sword-sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in snow Guang reached sword-peaked Old Man Mountain.

sentences.zh: 度黑崖，至鴉飛不到山。

translations.literal: Crossing Black Cliff, he reached Crow-Can't-Fly Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed Black Cliff to Crow-Can't-Fly Mountain.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，次歸來州，天大寒，然桂為薪，軍士皆凍墮指。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year he reached Guilai; the cold was extreme; they burned cassia for fuel and soldiers' fingers froze and fell off.
translations.idiomatic: In January at Guilai, soldiers froze; cassia fueled fires.

sentences.zh: 留四日，求乞弟不可得。

translations.literal: After four days they still could not find Qidi.
translations.idiomatic: After four days Qidi could not be found.

sentences.zh: 內侍麥文暼丙問廣軍事，廣曰：「賊未授首，當待罪。

translations.literal: Inner attendant Mai Wenjibing asked Guang about military affairs; Guang said: "The bandits have not been beheaded; I await guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Mai Wenjibing asked; Guang said he awaited guilt without Qidi's head.

sentences.zh: 」文暼丙乃出所受密詔曰：「大兵深入討賊，期在梟獲元惡。

translations.literal: Wenjibing then produced his secret edict: "The great army penetrates deep to attack bandits, expecting to capture the chief villain.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict allowed withdrawal if the nest was broken though Qidi escaped.

sentences.zh: 如已破其巢穴，雖未得乞弟，亦聽班師。

translations.literal: If their nest has been broken, though Qidi is not obtained, withdrawal is permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawal was permitted.

sentences.zh: 」軍中皆呼萬歲，曰：「天子居九重，明見萬里外。

translations.literal: The army all shouted ten thousand years, saying: "The Son of Heaven sits in nine layers and sees clearly ten thousand li beyond."
translations.idiomatic: The army cheered that the emperor saw ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 」乃以眾還。

translations.literal: " They then returned with the host.
translations.idiomatic: They marched home.

sentences.zh: 自納溪之役，師行凡四十日。

translations.literal: From the Naxi campaign, the army marched forty days in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Naxi campaign lasted forty days.

sentences.zh: 築樂共城、江門砦、梅嶺席帽溪堡，西達淯井，東道納溪，皆控制要害。

translations.literal: They built Le Gong city, Jiangmen Stockade, and Meiling Shimao Stream fort, west reaching Qijing, east reaching Naxi—all controlling strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: Le Gong, Jiangmen, and Meiling forts controlled Qijing and Naxi.

sentences.zh: 捷書聞，赦梓州路，以歸來州地賜羅氏鬼主。

translations.literal: When victory reports arrived, Zizhou circuit was pardoned; Guilai lands were granted the Luo Ghost Master.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhou was pardoned; Guilai went to the Luo Ghost Master.

sentences.zh: 乞弟既失土，窮甚，往來諸蠻間，無所依。

translations.literal: Qidi, having lost his land, was utterly destitute, wandering among the tribes with nowhere to rely.
translations.idiomatic: Landless Qidi wandered among tribes.

sentences.zh: 帝猶欲招來之，命知瀘州王光祖開諭，許以自新。

translations.literal: The emperor still wished to summon him; he ordered Luzhou prefect Wang Guangzu to open persuasion and permit renewal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still sought Qidi through Wang Guangzu.

sentences.zh: 會其死，於是羅始黨、鬥然、鬥更等諸酋請依十九姓團結，新收生界八姓、兩江夷族請依七姓團結，皆為義軍。

translations.literal: When he died, then Luoshidang, Houran, Hugeng, and other chiefs asked to join the nineteen surnames; newly received raw-border eight surnames and two-river Yi asked to join the seven surnames—all as righteous armies.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, chiefs joined nineteen and seven surname righteous armies.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 自是瀘夷震懾，不復為邊患。

translations.literal: From then on the Lu Yi were awed and no longer made deep border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi were awed and ceased major border trouble.

sentences.zh: 沙取祿路死，子鱉弊承襲。

translations.literal: When Shaqululu died, his son Biebi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Shaqululu's son Biebi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 政和五年，晏州夷卜漏叛，砦將高公老遁，招討使趙瘇討平之，授鱉弊西南夷界都大巡檢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenghe, Yanzhou Yi Bulou rebelled; stockade commander Gao Gonglao fled; pacification commissioner Zhao Zhen pacified them and appointed Biebi overall inspector of the southwestern Yi border.
translations.idiomatic: In 1115, Bulou rebelled; Zhao Zhen pacified him and made Biebi inspector.

sentences.zh: 事見《趙瘇傳》。

translations.literal: The matter is recorded in the "Biography of Zhao Zhen."
translations.idiomatic: See the biography of Zhao Zhen.
